adderall.japan: Japan treats amphetamine, the active ingredient in Adderall, as a prohibited substance for individual travellers. The Narcotics Control Department of Japan's health ministry says it cannot be brought in even with a foreign prescription, and that this applies to treatment use too. Do not pack it for a trip to Japan; talk to your doctor about an alternative before you travel.
adderall.united-arab-emirates: Adderall is prescribed for ADHD and narcolepsy, and its amphetamine is on the UAE list as Psychotropic Schedule II. That puts it in the group of controlled medicines the UAE does not allow to be imported freely. Under Federal Law by Decree No. 30 of 2021, bringing in narcotic or psychotropic substances is a crime unless it is regulated medical use, so keep your prescription or attested report with the box.
adderall.thailand: Thailand’s Food and Drug Administration sorts travellers’ controlled medicines by schedule, and its page does not say which schedule Adderall’s amphetamine falls under. If it is a psychotropic, the supply for up to 30 days needs only a certificate or prescription from your doctor; 31 to 90 days needs an FDA permit. If it is a narcotic, a permit is needed. Ask the FDA or your airline which applies before you travel.
adderall.panama: Panama’s rule, filed with the UN narcotics board in January 2025, does not name Adderall, so first find out whether amphetamine counts as a narcotic or a psychotropic there. For either group the filing allows up to 90 days, with a valid prescription, a doctor’s certificate endorsed by your home health authority, a copy of your ID and a case summary from your doctor dated within three months.
adderall.bahrain: Bahrain’s filing to the UN narcotics board allows only 7 days for both narcotics and psychotropics, which is the part to plan around if you take Adderall. You need a valid prescription, a doctor’s certificate endorsed by your home health authority and a certificate from Bahrain’s health authorities. The National Health Regulatory Authority answers questions on 17113222 or cunp@nhra.bh.
adderall.singapore: Amphetamine, the ingredient in Adderall, appears in Appendix A of Singapore’s Health Sciences Authority document guide, the list of controlled substances that need approval. Apply at least two weeks before arrival, in English only. The approval is tied to the arrival date you state, so a change of flight means a new application. Keep the approval email with you for officers at the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority.
adderall.united-kingdom: For Adderall, the UK Home Office’s personal-licence guidance works on a three-month rule. Amphetamine is a Schedule 2 drug, and a supply of up to three months that was prescribed and dispensed to you in your country of habitual residence needs no licence. Carry it yourself when you enter the UK. A letter from your prescriber, with the dose, strength and frequency and a signature with registration details, is what the Home Office recommends.
adderall.australia: Adderall is one of the medicines Australia’s Office of Drug Control names as covered by the traveller’s exemption. That means you may arrive with up to three months’ supply for yourself, or for an immediate family member travelling with you. Bring a prescription or a doctor’s letter with the medicine and dose, keep the original dispensing label on the pack, and tell Australian Border Force when you arrive.
adderall.hong-kong: Hong Kong’s Drug Office treats amphetamine, the ingredient in Adderall, as a dangerous drug. Even a visitor who is only passing through needs written approval from the Department of Health before arrival. The Drug Office says a complete application is normally processed in 10 working days, so apply well before you fly. Questions go to pharmgeneral@dh.gov.hk or 2572 2068.
adderall.canada: Health Canada names amphetamines among the commonly prescribed controlled substances you may carry in. The limit is a 90-day supply, worked out from the usual daily dose, and the medicine must come in the container your health care provider gave you. A doctor’s note is optional, but the label must show your name, the prescriber, the daily dose, the form, quantity and strength. Declare it to customs on arrival.
adderall.france: The ANSM does not name Adderall or amphetamine, but it mentions ADHD treatments among the medicines to check when travelling. For arriving in France, no transport attestation is required and the ANSM does not issue one. The original of your prescription is mandatory, ideally with an English translation if you travel on afterwards. Ask your doctor or pharmacist whether amphetamine counts as a narcotic.
adderall.netherlands: The Dutch government says ADHD medication falls under the Opium Act, on List I, and that this list gives active ingredients, not brand names. Adderall is not named, so ask your pharmacist whether amphetamine is on it. Opium Act medicines can enter the Netherlands only with an official certificate, so check that before you leave, rather than at the Dutch border.
adderall.united-states: In the United States the Drug Enforcement Administration generally decides whether a controlled substance, such as the amphetamine in Adderall, may be imported for personal use. The FDA coordinates with it on products under both agencies. Check the DEA website before you travel. The FDA’s own offer to foreign nationals, a 90-day supply, is made for drug products in general, not as a promise for controlled substances.
adderall.ukraine: Ukraine’s rule, filed with the UN narcotics board on 13 March 2024, names no drugs, so ask your doctor whether amphetamine counts as a narcotic or a psychotropic there. You need a valid prescription, a customs declaration and your passport. Limits: no more than 10 ampoules of narcotics, or 10 ampoules or 50 tablets of psychotropics. The Ministry of Health can be reached at moz@moz.gov.ua.
adderall.vietnam: Vietnam Customs states that visitors may bring medicines for their own treatment, within a quantity of up to 7 days’ use for narcotic drugs or up to 10 days’ use for psychotropic and precursor drugs, based on the dose in the prescription you carry. The page cites Decree 54/2017 and is dated 2019. It does not say which group amphetamine belongs to, so ask your doctor.
adderall.germany: Germany’s federal opium agency BfArM does not mention amphetamine or ADHD medicines on its travel page, so ask your doctor whether Adderall counts as a narcotic there. If it does, the Schengen rule applies: a certificate under Article 75, completed by your doctor and authenticated by the health authority before the trip, valid for at most 30 days. Only the person it was prescribed for may carry it.
adderall.ireland: Ireland’s Department of Health asks visitors from a Schengen country for an Article 75 certificate when a medicine contains a controlled drug in Schedule II or III of the Misuse of Drugs Regulations 2017. It is valid for up to 30 days and covers one drug. The page does not name amphetamine, so ask your doctor which schedule applies, and remember that customs has the final say.
adderall.israel: Israel’s Ministry of Health excludes narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances from the general 90-day allowance for personal medicines, and applies different rules to them. The page does not say where amphetamine falls, so ask your doctor whether Adderall counts. Read the Ministry’s guidance before you fly rather than relying on the general quantity.
adderall.kuwait: Kuwait’s filing to the UN narcotics board (10 March 2024) says only substances listed in schedules 2, 3 and 4 are allowed for travellers, and that narcotic drugs are currently not allowed at all. It names no drugs, so ask your doctor whether the amphetamine in Adderall is a narcotic or a psychotropic. For psychotropics the limit is 30 days, with the original prescription shown at Customs.
adderall.oman: Oman’s filing to the UN narcotics board (5 October 2016) gives the same 30-day limit for narcotic drugs and for psychotropic substances, so the class of the amphetamine in Adderall does not change the day limit. It also asks for a medical report from your treating institution, issued within the last six months, along with the prescription.
adderall.lebanon: Lebanon’s rule, filed with the UN narcotics board on 30 August 2014, allows 7 days of narcotic drugs and 30 days of psychotropic substances, so the class of Adderall’s amphetamine decides how much you may bring. The filing also requires the approval of the Department of Narcotics at the Ministry of Public Health, and a medical report explaining your case.
adderall.peru: Peru’s filing to the UN narcotics board (27 January 2025) allows narcotic drugs for up to 5 days only, while psychotropic substances may be carried in the amount of the medical prescription. Which group the amphetamine in Adderall belongs to is for your doctor to confirm. Substances on Lists I-A and I-B of annex 2 of Supreme Decree No. 023-2001-SA are prohibited.
adderall.kenya: Kenya’s filing to the UN narcotics board (18 March 2024) gives the same limit for both groups: 30 days for narcotic drugs and 30 days for psychotropic substances. The amphetamine in Adderall is not named, but the day limit stays the same either way. Bring a valid prescription and show the original at Customs. The Pharmacy and Poisons Board is the contact.
adderall.seychelles: Seychelles’ filing to the UN narcotics board (4 December 2013) allows 30 days of narcotic drugs but 90 days of psychotropic substances, so the class of Adderall’s amphetamine matters. It asks for a doctor’s certificate endorsed in your home country and a certificate from the Seychelles health authorities. Flunitrazepam is the one substance the filing lists as prohibited.
adderall.morocco: Morocco’s filing to the UN narcotics board, dated 10 August 2026, sets no day limit for controlled medicines but asks for more paper than most countries. Beyond a prescription, you need a patient’s written request, and for a medicine not sold in Morocco an authorization of release for consumption issued by the Moroccan health authorities. Ask your doctor how amphetamine is classed there.
adderall.luxembourg: Luxembourg’s filing to the UN narcotics board (7 March 2024) asks for a copy of the valid prescription and a doctor’s certificate endorsed by the health authorities of your country of residence, and states that the Schengen agreement applies. It gives no day or quantity limit and names no drugs, so ask your doctor whether the amphetamine in Adderall counts as a narcotic.
adderall.malta: Malta’s filing to the UN narcotics board, dated 3 January 2017, asks only for a valid medical prescription and says the Schengen agreement applies. It states no day or quantity limit and names no drugs, so ask your doctor whether amphetamine is controlled. The Superintendent of Public Health at St Luke’s Hospital is the contact.
adderall.argentina: The Argentine government page on Mercosur Resolution 66/2000 does not name Adderall or amphetamine, so it is not confirmed whether it counts as a psychotropic there. If it does, the rule is a legalised prescription authorised by the health authority, showing the active ingredient, strength, quantity and dose. The page gives no quantity limit, so ask ANMAT before you fly.
adderall.austria: Austria's health ministry does not list Adderall by name, but it says medicines with addictive or psychotropic substances face strict checks and that unlawful possession can lead to prosecution. Up to 5 days you can bring them with proof of need; up to 30 days you need your home doctor's prescription and no more than 30 days' supply. Over 30 days, an Austrian doctor can prescribe.
adderall.belgium: Belgium's medicines agency lists ADHD medicines with methylphenidate as an example of controlled medicines, but Adderall's amphetamine is not named in the rule we could confirm. If it counts, you need an official proof of prescription: a Schengen declaration validated by your home authority, or from outside Schengen a prescription or government-validated certificate. Maximum is 3 months and it cannot be posted.
adderall.brazil: Brazil's Anvisa baggage page has no separate rule for controlled substances, so nothing there says whether Adderall's amphetamine is allowed. The Federal Revenue lists narcotic substances among prohibited goods and medicines among goods with restrictions. Because the rule is unclear, ask Anvisa or customs in writing before you travel and carry your prescription.
adderall.bulgaria: The Bulgarian Customs Agency FAQ does not name Adderall. For medicines with narcotic substances from the listed groups it allows foreigners staying or in transit to hold them only for treatment, no more than 30 days' worth, with a document from the authorities of the country that prescribed it. Amphetamine's status on the lists is not confirmed here, so ask Bulgarian customs.
adderall.chile: Chile's ISP says there is no special health rule for medicines carried by travellers, so Adderall follows the general rules: a dated prescription or medical certificate signed by a doctor, not older than 6 months, showing the daily dose and length of treatment. It should fit the treatment and be in the original packaging. The guide gives no separate list of controlled substances.
adderall.colombia: Article 59 of Colombia's Resolution 826 of 2003 covers narcotics on Lists I and II of the 1961 Convention and psychotropics on Lists II, III and IV of the 1971 Convention. Adderall's amphetamine is not named in the article, so confirm its list with a pharmacist. If covered, you may carry a standard 30-day treatment and must show a copy of the prescription.
adderall.croatia: Croatia's Customs Administration allows medicine containing narcotics for personal use only in the quantity for up to 5 days, with medical documents: copies of prescriptions, an illness history or a certified physician's certificate. Amphetamine is not named on the page. People in addiction substitution therapy or treated for a malignant disease may bring up to 15 days.
adderall.cyprus: Cyprus's Pharmaceutical Services say visitors who carry small quantities of internationally controlled medicines for their own treatment need a permit from the Inspection Department. Amphetamine is not named in what we could read. The application form and traveller guidelines are on the ministry's website.
adderall.czechia: The Czech Customs Administration page on addictive substances does not name Adderall. It says importing addictive substances needs an import permit from the Ministry of Health, plus an export permit from the origin country where that country requires one, with exemptions in sections 20(2) and 21(2) of Act 167/1998. The page does not explain those exemptions. Customs phone: +420 261 331 111.
adderall.denmark: Denmark's Medicines Agency allows medicine with euphoriant substances from lists B, C, D and E only up to a 30-day personal supply, for your own treatment. Medicine with list A substances may not be brought in by private persons. Adderall is not named on the page; check the Executive Order's schedules. Agency phone 44 88 95 95, email dkma@dkma.dk.
adderall.dominican-republic: The Dominican customs Manual del Viajero says that for controlled or psychotropic substances you must present the medical prescription that justifies their use during your stay. Adderall is not named, and the page does not explain which substances count. The same site lists drugs and psychotropic substances among restricted items without explaining how that fits, so confirm with customs.
adderall.egypt: Article 73 of Egypt's customs regulations lists what is part of a tourist's duty-free luggage: used clothing, objects carried on a trip, and medicine for personal use at the discretion of the competent control authority. It sets no quantity, document list or separate rule for narcotic or psychotropic medicine, and Adderall is not named, so the officer decides. Carry the prescription and ask the Egyptian Customs Authority before you fly.
adderall.estonia: Estonia's Tax and Customs Board lets narcotic or psychotropic medicine in without a permit as one retail package of up to 30 units or 25 ml, with a doctor's notice or prescription copy. More, up to 30 days' treatment, needs State Agency of Medicines authorisation. Amphetamine is not named; the agency is at +372 737 4140.
adderall.ethiopia: The EFDA's May 2023 guideline does not name Adderall and gives no separate narcotic rule. It says a pre-import permit is not required for medical products imported for personal use, and at the port the product information and quantity are checked against your prescription paper. Bring a prescription from an authorised health professional.
adderall.fiji: Fiji's March 2024 medicines guideline does not name Adderall. Its traveller rule is that anyone entering, leaving or transiting Fiji with medicine for personal use must show at the border that it was legally prescribed and supplied to them. Under section 11 of the Illicit Drugs Control Act 2004, a controlled drug lawfully prescribed may be possessed for no more than one month.
adderall.finland: Finland counts medicines mainly affecting the central nervous system or psychotropic medicines as narcotics. You may bring up to 30 days' supply from a Schengen country, and no more than 14 days' from a non-Schengen country. Adderall is not named. A pharmacy Schengen certificate is needed inside the Schengen area. Importing illegal narcotics is treated as a drug offence.
adderall.georgia: Georgia's customs brochure does not name amphetamine, but it names methamphetamine and says all other narcotic or psychotropic substances in Georgian law are included. Import needs medical documents: a prescription copy translated into English and approved by the authority of the country you travel from, the doctor's certificate, and a sealed confirmation. The supply is limited to 31 days.
adderall.greece: The Schengen decision Greece relies on speaks only of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances in general, and Adderall is not named. For residents of a Schengen state going to another Schengen state, a certificate from the national authority is needed, valid at most 30 days and for one drug each. It gives no rule for travellers from outside Schengen.
adderall.hungary: Hungary's rule asks you to show valid documents at the customs and police check if you carry a controlled substance. Adderall is not named. For narcotic drugs, up to 3 days' treatment needs only a GP's international certificate, and 3 to 90 days needs an official certificate; for psychotropics, up to 30 days with a GP certificate.
adderall.iceland: The Icelandic Medicines Agency does not name Adderall. For narcotic or psychotropic medicines it allows 30 days' supply, measured in defined daily doses, from outside the EEA. From the EEA, non-residents may bring 30 days, while residents with medicine obtained abroad may bring 7 days, or 30 with a declaration from a doctor licensed in Iceland.
adderall.india: India's customs traveller guide lists narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances among prohibited imports, and the medicines notice of the CDSCO gives no separate rule for them. Adderall is not named in either. Because the position is unclear, do not assume a prescription is enough; ask the Indian customs or the nearest Indian mission before you travel.
adderall.indonesia: BPOM's passenger leaflet under Regulation 28 of 2023 does not name Adderall. It says narcotic medicines are not permitted in passenger belongings, while psychotropic medicines need a doctor's prescription and may be carried up to 60 days of treatment. Customs inspects and may release them in full, in part or not at all. BPOM contact: was.sas.bbo@pom.go.id.
adderall.italy: Italy excludes medicines with narcotic or psychotropic substances from its general rule that carried medicines have no specific requirements. Adderall is not named. Travellers from Schengen countries need an Article 75 certificate valid 30 days, issued on a doctor's prescription, and without authorisation narcotic drugs can be confiscated by customs.
adderall.jamaica: Jamaica Customs says items that need an import permit must get one from the Ministry of Health, and that applicable duties and taxes are charged. The foreign ministry page asks for a special permit for prescription drugs, applied for with a physician's letter, a prescription copy and flight details. Adderall is not named, and no quantity limit is given.
adderall.jordan: Jordan's regulation for travellers, filed with the INCB in 2025, covers narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances together: for personal use only, no more than six months and no more than the quantity in the international passenger authority manual. Adderall is not named. You must get authorisation from the Jordan Food and Drug Administration's control department.
adderall.latvia: Latvia's State Agency of Medicines requires, for medicines with substances in Schedule II or III entering from a Schengen country, a certificate from the competent authority of the country you come from. Adderall is not named. From outside Schengen, no permit is needed for up to 14 days (Schedule II) or 30 days (Schedule III) with a prescription.
adderall.lithuania: Lithuanian customs lists narcotic medicines (buprenorphine, fentanyl, methadone, morphine, pethidine, tramadol) and psychotropic ones (alprazolam, diazepam, clonazepam, lorazepam, zolpidem, phenobarbital, higher-dose codeine) as examples, and Adderall is not among them. Any such medicine must be in original packaging, in your name, for personal use only and not more than your certificate or prescription states.
adderall.malaysia: Malaysia's Traveller's Guide says prescription medicines containing dangerous drugs must be declared at the border on arrival, with a valid prescription or doctor's letter in English or translated, showing the medicine name, dose and quantity. Adderall is not named; the First Schedule of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 lists the dangerous drugs.
adderall.maldives: Maldives Customs lists narcotics and psychotropic substances as prohibited goods, but also says a valid prescription from a registered medical practitioner is required to import controlled drugs for personal use. Adderall is not named. Because the two statements pull in different directions, ask Maldives Customs before you travel.
adderall.mauritius: The Mauritius Revenue Authority's rule for controlled medicines is that you need approval from the Government Pharmacist of the Ministry of Health and Quality of Life, a legible prescription from your doctor, the medicine in its original containers, and no more than a one-month supply. Adderall is not named, so ask whether amphetamine counts.
adderall.mexico: Mexico's customs agency ANAM says that for psychotropic substances you must show the corresponding medical prescription. Adderall is not named, and the page does not say which substances count as psychotropic. A separate ANAM page on goods you cannot bring in lists narcotics (estupefacientes), so confirm with customs.
adderall.nepal: We found no official or unofficial source for Nepal on Adderall, so this page gives no limits or document list. The general rule most countries follow is that amphetamine-type medicines need advance approval and the prescription. Check with Nepal's Department of Drug Administration (dda.gov.np) or a Nepali embassy before you fly.
adderall.nigeria: We found no official source for Nigeria on Adderall, so this page gives no limit and no permit rule. Amphetamine-type medicines often need approval first in other countries. Carry the prescription, keep the original packaging, and ask NAFDAC (nafdac.gov.ng), Nigerian customs (customs.gov.ng) or a Nigerian embassy before you fly.
adderall.norway: Norway's Medical Products Agency (NOMA) does not name Adderall. Medicines with narcotic substances must be prescribed for you and documented, and declared in the red zone. Without a Norwegian address you can bring up to 30 days' use with a prescription copy or doctor's letter; for more, apply to NOMA beforehand. Email narkotikakontroll@dmp.no.
adderall.philippines: The 2015 joint circular of the DOH, FDA and Bureau of Customs does not name Adderall. It says dangerous drugs, controlled precursors and similar substances are subject to the Dangerous Drugs Board and the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency, and gives no traveller allowance for them. Ask PDEA before you carry amphetamine.
adderall.poland: Poland's Chief Pharmaceutical Inspectorate asks for a document before you carry any medicine on Poland's list of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances. Adderall is not named in what we could confirm. The document is issued within 15 days before you cross the border, for no more than 30 days, one per product, and covers only carrying it yourself.
adderall.portugal: Portugal's Decree-Law 15/93, Article 13, published by Infarmed, lets people crossing the border carry substances in tables I-A, II-B, II-C, III and IV for their own use, up to 30 days of treatment, with a medical document justifying the need. Adderall is not named in the part we could confirm.
adderall.qatar: Qatar's Ministry of Public Health asks travellers arriving or leaving with controlled medicines to obtain a permit through its electronic system with a valid prescription. Adderall is not named. Applications are approved or rejected within three working days once all requirements are met; apply at least five working days before you travel.
adderall.romania: Romanian Customs says that when you enter from a non-EU state you must declare in writing, in every case, drugs or psychotropic substances and medicines containing narcotic or psychotropic substances. Adderall is not named. Not declaring or declaring wrongly can be fined or prosecuted, and the goods are held for confiscation. No quantity limit or document list is given.
adderall.russia: Russia's Federal Customs Service says medicines with narcotic or psychotropic substances may be brought in for personal use only on medical grounds, with documents naming the medicine and quantity. They must be in Russian or carry a notarised Russian translation, and be declared in writing. Adderall is not named; they may not be posted.
adderall.saudi-arabia: Saudi Arabia's SFDA says travellers arriving or leaving with controlled drugs containing narcotic or psychotropic substances need a clearance permit, applied for online in the SFDA Controlled Drugs System. Adderall is not named. Upload a prescription, a medical report and ID, and give the trade name, active ingredient, concentration and quantity for each medicine.
adderall.serbia: Serbia's Customs Administration says medicines containing controlled psychoactive substances need approval for personal import from the competent ministry, and links only to the Ministry of Health site. Adderall is not named. Ordinary medicines for regular therapy up to 15 days need no medical opinion. The page does not say whether the psychoactive rule applies within 15 days.
adderall.slovakia: Slovakia's 2007 filing with the INCB does not name Adderall. For psychotropic substances it allows 7 days for Schedule II and 30 days for Schedules III and IV of the 1971 Convention, with a valid medical prescription, and the Schengen agreement applies. Contact: Ministry of Health, Limbova 2, Bratislava, tel. +421 2 59373 111.
adderall.slovenia: Slovenia's Financial Administration says illicit drugs used as medicines may be carried within the Schengen area with a medical certificate issued or endorsed by a competent authority of your country of permanent residence. Adderall is not named. Medicines in general need proof of prescription and are limited to three weeks.
adderall.south-africa: SAHPRA's June 2022 guideline does not name Adderall. Regulation 8(1) lets a person entering South Africa hold a Schedule 3, 4, 5 or 6 medicine for personal use, up to one month's supply, with a valid prescription, a prescriber's certificate naming the medicine and quantity and the prescriber's address, and your residence particulars recorded at the port of entry.
adderall.south-korea: South Korea's MFDS requires handling approval for anyone entering with narcotic or psychotropic drugs for their own treatment, Korean or foreign. Adderall is not named, so confirm whether amphetamine counts. The requirement has applied since 23 October 2009, and online applications have been accepted since 27 December 2024.
adderall.spain: Spain's AEMPS requires travellers entering with narcotic or psychotropic medicines to request a permit from its Narcotics and Psychotropics Area, authorising them to carry the medicine for their own treatment. Adderall is not named. The page gives no validity period; for general medicines you may be asked for a prescription or medical report.
adderall.cambodia: We found no official or unofficial source for Cambodia on Adderall, so this page states no limit and no permit rule. Amphetamine-type medicines are controlled in many countries and often need approval first. Carry the prescription and the original packaging, and ask the Cambodian embassy or Ministry of Health before you travel.
adderall.costa-rica: Costa Rica's Drug Surveillance Board (JVD) lets treated travellers bring in or take out one month of treatment for personal use. Adderall is not named. Documents: an ID copy, the prescription, the doctor's clinical summary issued within three months, and the purchase invoice if any, all translated into Spanish.
adderall.cuba: Cuba's 2022 filing with the INCB does not name amphetamine. It requires a valid prescription, a doctor's certificate endorsed by your country's health authorities and a certificate from Cuban health authorities. Psychotropic substances are allowed for your stay up to a maximum of 30 days with official medical documentation.
adderall.sri-lanka: Sri Lanka's NMRA does not name Adderall. It says medicines in Schedule III are not permitted, and you should check with the NMRA whether your medicine is listed. Ordinary personal medicine may be carried without approval for your stay or 90 days, whichever is less. Contact +94 11 2698896.
adderall.sweden: Swedish Customs says narcotic or doping medicines may be brought only for medical purposes and personal use, which you must prove with a prescription, pharmacy label or doctor's certificate. Adderall is not named. In some cases a Schengen certificate stating the prescriber, the patient and the dosage is needed. Customs: +46 771 520 520.
adderall.switzerland: Swissmedic does not name Adderall. Medicines containing narcotics may be imported up to a 30-day treatment supply, ideally in hand luggage and original packaging, with a certificate, one per medicine. Stays beyond 30 days: importing more than a month is not possible, and no exceptions are made.
adderall.taiwan: Taiwan's customs page does not name Adderall. For controlled drugs it allows up to a 6-month supply with a prescription or supporting document, and clearance needs a statement certified by the Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA). Check on the TFDA site whether amphetamine counts as controlled. TFDA phone: +886 2 2787 8000.
adderall.turkey: The Turkish customs information page does not name Adderall and has no separate rule for narcotics. It lets passengers bring medication for personal treatment, with them or sent one month before or three months after arrival. Customs must see a document such as a medical report or prescription confirming you need it during your stay.
adderall.new-zealand: New Zealand's Medsafe lets you carry up to three months' supply of a prescription medicine that is not a controlled drug, and one month of a controlled drug carried in person and declared on the arrival card. Whether amphetamine is controlled is shown in Medsafe's classification database, which we did not read, so look it up under the ingredient name.
adderall.china: Amphetamine is not shown in the part of China's 2025 psychotropic catalogue we read, where methylphenidate is Category I and drugs such as zolpidem and alprazolam are Category II. Shanghai Customs asks you to declare controlled medicine, carry a prescription or diagnosis certificate and a reasonable personal quantity; officers decide on site.

vyvanse.japan: Vyvanse contains lisdexamfetamine, which Japan's Narcotics Control Department lists among the raw materials of stimulants. Medicines in that group need an import certificate before you arrive, and you show it to Customs. The page names no amount that is allowed without permission, so the rule applies to any quantity. The application needs a doctor's certificate issued within the last three months.
vyvanse.united-arab-emirates: Vyvanse is used for ADHD, and the UAE controlled-medicines list files its lisdexamfetamine as Psychotropic Schedule II. For travellers, the list sets one limit: enough for the length of your stay, with three months as the ceiling. The paperwork it asks for is a prescription or an attested report from your health provider. Plan the quantity from your return date, not from what the pharmacy hands you.
vyvanse.singapore: Lisdexamfetamine, the active ingredient of Vyvanse, is named on Appendix A of Singapore’s HSA document guide, so it needs approval before you travel. The application wants medical papers (a pharmacy label, prescription or doctor’s letter with your details, the dose and the total quantity) plus clear photographs of the product showing name, strength and dispensed quantity. Apply two weeks ahead, in English.
vyvanse.united-kingdom: Vyvanse is lisdexamfetamine, a Schedule 2 drug in the UK. Under the Home Office policy you may bring up to three months’ supply without a licence if it was lawfully prescribed to you where you live. The Home Office suggests a doctor’s letter showing you are not above three months, worked out from your travel dates and the quantity. If you need more, you must ask by email a month before travel.

sudafed.japan: Sudafed contains pseudoephedrine, which Japan’s Narcotics Control Department lists with the raw materials of stimulants. For products that fall under this rule, an import certificate is required before entry and you show it to Customs. Whether your Sudafed product falls under it depends on its strength, as the rule above explains. If it does, apply at least 14 days before you fly, to the office that covers your home area or your arrival airport.
sudafed.united-arab-emirates: Sudafed is a decongestant, but its pseudoephedrine is on the UAE list as controlled under the 1988 UN Convention. That makes it a restricted item, even though it is sold over the counter in many countries. You may carry the quantity for your stay, up to three months, with a prescription or an attested report. Do not assume a pharmacy pack from home is fine.
sudafed.thailand: The FDA page for Thailand does not say whether the pseudoephedrine in Sudafed is treated as a controlled drug, so the card above stays conditional. If it is controlled, the rules are the FDA’s: a 30-day supply with a doctor’s paper for psychotropics, a permit for 31 to 90 days or for narcotics. Apply for permits online, at least 15 days before you travel.
sudafed.panama: Panama’s filing to the UN narcotics board names no drugs, so it does not say whether Sudafed’s pseudoephedrine is covered. If your product counts as controlled, the filing allows up to 90 days and asks for a prescription, an endorsed doctor’s certificate, a copy of your ID and a case summary dated within the last three months.
sudafed.bahrain: Bahrain’s filing does not list drugs, so it does not say if Sudafed is controlled. If your product is, the filing allows 7 days and asks for a valid prescription, a doctor’s certificate endorsed in your home country and a certificate from Bahrain’s health authorities. The National Health Regulatory Authority can confirm on 17113222.
sudafed.singapore: Pseudoephedrine is not named on Appendix A of Singapore’s HSA document guide. For medicines outside that list and not prohibited, the HSA allows up to three months’ supply with a copy of a valid prescription or doctor’s letter from your country of residence. Keep Sudafed in its original container, labelled with your name, the medicine and the quantity.
sudafed.new-zealand: New Zealand’s Ministry of Health says medicines containing pseudoephedrine are controlled drugs, so Sudafed follows the controlled-drug route: declare it on the arrival card and carry it yourself, in its original labelled container. Medsafe puts the limit for controlled drugs at one month’s supply, and says they cannot be imported by mail. It is for your own condition only, not for friends or family.
sudafed.canada: Health Canada treats pseudoephedrine as a Class A precursor, which is why Sudafed has its own rule. You may bring it to treat a medical condition for yourself or for a person you are responsible for who is travelling with you. The product must be packaged and labelled as a consumer product and hold no more than 3 g of pseudoephedrine in total. The same rule applies when you leave Canada.
sudafed.france: The ANSM does not mention pseudoephedrine in its travel page, so ask your doctor or pharmacist whether Sudafed is classed as a narcotic-type medicine in France. The page does state that travellers entering France need no attestation, and that carrying the original prescription is mandatory. For customs questions it refers to the French customs website.
sudafed.netherlands: Pseudoephedrine is not mentioned on the Dutch government’s page about medicines abroad. The general rule for the Netherlands is that most medicines may be brought in if you can show they are for your own use, and that Opium Act medicines need an official certificate. Ask your pharmacist whether Sudafed falls under that Act, and keep it in its original packaging.
sudafed.united-states: The FDA page on personal importation does not mention pseudoephedrine, so Sudafed does not get a ruling there. The page says that for controlled substances the DEA generally decides, and that the FDA’s 90-day allowance for foreign nationals covers drug products in general. Ask your pharmacist whether your product is controlled, then check the DEA site.
sudafed.ukraine: Ukraine’s filing to the INCB does not say whether pseudoephedrine is controlled, so Sudafed’s status is for your pharmacist to confirm. If it is, the documents are a valid prescription, a customs declaration and a passport, and the limits are 10 ampoules of narcotics or 10 ampoules or 50 tablets of psychotropics. The filing is dated 13 March 2024.
sudafed.vietnam: Vietnam’s Customs page allows up to 10 days’ use of psychotropic and precursor drugs for your own treatment, based on the prescribed dose, and 7 days for narcotics. It names no drugs, so ask your pharmacist how Sudafed’s pseudoephedrine is classed there. Carry the prescription that shows the dose.
sudafed.germany: BfArM’s page for travellers deals with narcotic drugs and says nothing about pseudoephedrine, so Sudafed is not covered there. If your pharmacist says your product contains a controlled drug, the Schengen certificate rule applies: Article 75, 30 days at most, one certificate for each drug, signed by your doctor and authenticated by the health authority.
sudafed.ireland: Pseudoephedrine is not named in the Irish Department of Health’s travel rule. Ask your pharmacist whether Sudafed falls in Schedule II or III of the Misuse of Drugs Regulations 2017. If it does, a Schengen visitor needs an Article 75 certificate of up to 30 days. Customs makes the final decision on what you carry in.
sudafed.israel: The Israeli Ministry of Health page does not mention pseudoephedrine. Its general rule is a maximum 90-day quantity, based on the recommended dosage, for your own needs, with narcotics and psychotropics excluded. Ask your pharmacist whether Sudafed counts as either. Keep it in the original packaging.
sudafed.kuwait: Kuwait’s filing to the INCB does not mention pseudoephedrine, so Sudafed’s status is for your pharmacist to confirm. The filing sets 30 days for psychotropic substances in schedules 2, 3 and 4, with the original prescription shown at Customs, and says narcotic drugs are currently not allowed. A second contact at the ministry is aljragh@moh.gov.kw.
sudafed.oman: Oman’s filing does not say whether pseudoephedrine is controlled, so ask your pharmacist about Sudafed. If it is, the filing gives 30 days for narcotics and for psychotropics, with a valid prescription and a medical report no more than six months old, from the institution treating you. Oman points to its guidance for importing medicinal products for personal use.
sudafed.lebanon: Lebanon’s INCB filing says nothing about pseudoephedrine, so ask your pharmacist if Sudafed counts as controlled. If it does, you need approval from the Department of Narcotics at the Ministry of Public Health, a valid prescription with the dispensing pharmacy’s stamp, an identity document and a medical report. The limits are 7 days for narcotics and 30 for psychotropics.
sudafed.peru: Peru’s filing to the UN narcotics board does not mention pseudoephedrine, so ask your pharmacist about Sudafed. If it counts as a controlled medicine, you need a valid prescription, a doctor’s certificate endorsed by your home health authority and the original prescription at Customs. The limits are 5 days for narcotics and the prescribed amount for psychotropics.
sudafed.kenya: Kenya’s filing does not say whether pseudoephedrine is controlled, so ask your pharmacist about Sudafed. For controlled medicines, the rule is 30 days of supply for narcotics and for psychotropics, with a valid prescription and the original shown to Customs. The filing is dated 18 March 2024.
sudafed.seychelles: Seychelles’ INCB filing does not mention pseudoephedrine, so ask your pharmacist about Sudafed. If it is controlled, the filing allows 30 days of narcotics and 90 days of psychotropics, with a prescription, a doctor’s certificate endorsed in your home country and a certificate from the Seychelles health authorities.
sudafed.morocco: Morocco’s INCB filing does not mention pseudoephedrine, so Sudafed’s status is a question for your pharmacist. If it is controlled there, the filing’s documents apply: prescription, a doctor’s certificate endorsed at home, a certificate from the Moroccan health authorities, the patient’s written request and, for medicines not sold in Morocco, an authorization of release for consumption.
sudafed.luxembourg: Pseudoephedrine does not appear in Luxembourg’s INCB filing, so ask your pharmacist whether Sudafed is controlled. If it is, you need a copy of the valid prescription and a doctor’s certificate endorsed by your home health authority, under the Schengen agreement. The filing sets no day or quantity limit.
sudafed.malta: Malta’s filing does not mention pseudoephedrine, so ask your pharmacist if Sudafed is controlled. The filing’s rule for controlled medicines is a valid medical prescription under the Schengen agreement, with no day or quantity limit stated. The filing is dated January 2017, so check for newer guidance.
sudafed.argentina: The Argentine government page does not say whether pseudoephedrine is a narcotic or psychotropic substance, so the Resolution 66/2000 rules may or may not apply to Sudafed. Where they do, a legalised prescription with active ingredient, concentration and dose is required. For a simple cold remedy, ask a pharmacist or ANMAT first rather than assuming either way.
sudafed.austria: Whether pseudoephedrine falls under Austria's addictive-substance rules is not stated on the ministry page. If Sudafed is treated as an ordinary medicine, your usual personal needs, up to three retail packs of the smallest size, need no permit. If it is treated as controlled, the prescription rules for 5 to 30 days apply. Ask a pharmacist or the ministry.
sudafed.belgium: Pseudoephedrine is not among the examples Belgium gives for controlled medicines, so whether Sudafed needs paperwork is not confirmed here. If it is on the narcotic and psychotropic list, you need a Schengen declaration or a prescription as proof, limited to 3 months of treatment, and it cannot be posted. Ask a pharmacist or FAMHP if unsure.
sudafed.brazil: Brazil's baggage rules do not state whether pseudoephedrine is treated as a restricted medicine or something stricter. Anvisa's general test is personal use: a quantity that fits your stay and treatment and does not suggest trade. A signed prescription may be requested if the amount does not fit. Check with Anvisa if you plan to carry more than a few days of Sudafed.
sudafed.bulgaria: The Bulgarian Customs Agency FAQ does not say whether pseudoephedrine is on its narcotic lists. If a medicine is, you may keep it only for treatment, with no more than 30 days' supply and a document from the authorities of the prescribing country. Otherwise it is an ordinary medicine. Check with customs if you are unsure.
sudafed.chile: Chile's ISP guide does not single out pseudoephedrine. Customs treats medicines for you or direct family as baggage in the quantities of the prescription, and for over-the-counter products asks you to bring only what you need for your stay. Raw materials, such as unlabelled powders or liquids, are banned.
sudafed.colombia: Pseudoephedrine is not named in Colombia's Article 59, so whether Sudafed is covered is not stated. The article's rule for medicines on the 1961 and 1971 Convention lists is up to 30 days of standard treatment with a copy of the prescription. If you are unsure which group it is in, ask a Colombian pharmacist before you fly.
sudafed.croatia: The Croatian customs page does not say whether pseudoephedrine counts as a narcotic. If Sudafed is an ordinary medicine, you may bring the quantity needed for treatment, up to one month, with an illness history or physician's certificate, and it must be approved in the manufacturer's country. If it counts as a narcotic, the limit is 5 days.
sudafed.cyprus: Whether pseudoephedrine counts as an internationally controlled medicine in Cyprus is not stated in the text we could read. If it does, the Inspection Department of the Pharmaceutical Services must issue a permit for small quantities for your own treatment. If you are unsure, ask the Ministry of Health before you travel.
sudafed.czechia: The Czech customs page does not say whether pseudoephedrine counts as an addictive substance. If it is an ordinary medicine, only the quantity matching your normal personal need for your stay is allowed when it was sold outside the European Community. If it is addictive, a Ministry of Health import permit is normally needed.
sudafed.denmark: The Danish Medicines Agency page does not say whether pseudoephedrine is euphoriant. Only if it is on one of the Danish lists do the euphoriant rules apply: a 30-day personal supply from lists B to E, with a prescription or Schengen certificate, and nothing at all from list A. The agency answers questions by phone, 44 88 95 95, 9:00 to 15:00.
sudafed.dominican-republic: The Dominican customs manual does not say whether pseudoephedrine is a controlled substance. Medicines for personal use are allowed and no quantity limit is stated; controlled or psychotropic ones need the prescription justifying their use during your stay. It also lists medicines among items that may need a customs declaration.
sudafed.egypt: Pseudoephedrine is not mentioned in Egypt's Article 73, which covers medicine for personal use at the control authority's discretion and sits in a list with clothing, cameras and up to 10,000 Egyptian pounds of new items. No rule or limit is given for Sudafed, so keep it in its original packaging and bring any prescription.
sudafed.estonia: Whether pseudoephedrine is narcotic or psychotropic in Estonia is not stated by the customs board. If not, the ordinary limit applies: up to 10 different medicines and 5 retail packages of each. If it is, one package of up to 30 units with a doctor's notice or prescription copy. The agency's contact is +372 737 4140.
sudafed.ethiopia: Pseudoephedrine is not addressed in the EFDA guideline. For personal-use medicine it requires no pre-import permit; at the port, inspectors check the product and quantity against your prescription. The prescription from an authorised health professional should state the type, description and quantity. Ask the EFDA if unsure.
sudafed.fiji: Fiji's guideline does not say whether pseudoephedrine counts as a controlled drug. Any medicine you carry as a traveller needs evidence of lawful prescription and supply at the border. If it is a controlled drug, the Illicit Drugs Control Act 2004 limit of one month applies.
sudafed.finland: Finland's travel page does not say whether pseudoephedrine is classed as a narcotic. As an ordinary medicine, up to a year's supply from the EEA or three months from elsewhere is allowed if licensed where bought. If it is a narcotic, 30 days from the Schengen area or 14 days from outside. Ask Fimea, whose contact page is on fimea.fi.
sudafed.georgia: Pseudoephedrine is named in Georgia's customs brochure alongside ephedrine and norephedrine and their combined preparations, so Sudafed is treated as a controlled medicine. You need an English prescription copy approved by the authority of the country you travel from, the doctor's certificate, and a signed, sealed confirmation; supply is limited to 31 days.
sudafed.greece: Whether pseudoephedrine is covered is not stated in the Schengen decision Greece cites, which names no drug at all. If a medicine is classed as narcotic or psychotropic, a Schengen traveller needs the Article 75 certificate for up to 30 days. Otherwise it is an ordinary medicine. Ask a pharmacist or the Greek Medicines Department.
sudafed.hungary: Hungary's rule does not say whether pseudoephedrine is a controlled substance. Medicines that are not controlled need no special permit or certificate to enter. If it is controlled, carry documents: a GP's international certificate for the shorter periods, an official certificate for longer ones, up to 90 days.
sudafed.iceland: The Icelandic Medicines Agency page does not say whether pseudoephedrine is narcotic or psychotropic. If it is not, a general medicine is allowed up to 100 days' supply from outside the EEA, or a year from within it. If it is, the limit is 30 days. A document such as the prescription or a label must be shown on request.
sudafed.india: Pseudoephedrine is not named in India's customs guide. For ordinary medicines the CDSCO notice allows small quantities for exclusive personal use, up to 100 average doses of any single drug, declared if customs asks. Whether Sudafed is treated as a psychotropic substance is not stated, so check first.
sudafed.indonesia: BPOM's leaflet does not classify pseudoephedrine. Without a prescription, solid medicines may be carried up to 30 pieces per product and semi-solid, liquid or aerosol ones up to 3; with a prescription, up to 90 days of treatment. If it is psychotropic, 60 days. Customs makes the final release decision.
sudafed.italy: Italy's guidance does not say whether pseudoephedrine is a narcotic or psychotropic substance. If it is not, the general rule applies and a carried medicine has no specific requirements. If it is, an Article 75 certificate valid for 30 days is needed from Schengen countries. Ask a pharmacist.
sudafed.jamaica: Jamaica's pages do not say whether pseudoephedrine needs the prescription-drug permit. If Sudafed is treated as a prescription drug, you need a special permit from the Ministry of Health Pharmaceutical and Regulatory Division. Duties and taxes can apply either way. Jamaica Customs head office: 876 922 5140.
sudafed.jordan: Whether pseudoephedrine falls under Jordan's controlled-medicine regulation is not stated in what we could read. If it does, personal use only, no more than six months, with authorisation from the Jordan Food and Drug Administration's control department. If you are unsure, ask them before travelling.
sudafed.latvia: The Latvian agency does not say whether pseudoephedrine is in Schedule II or III. If it is not, the ordinary rules apply: original packaging, an identifiable manufacturer, a receipt, and a written statement of personal use above three packs. If it is, a certificate or the 14 and 30-day limits apply.
sudafed.lithuania: Lithuania's customs page does not list pseudoephedrine among narcotic or psychotropic medicines. If it is an ordinary medicine, you may bring up to 10 packs at a time without a doctor's certificate, once per calendar month, and the limit does not apply to narcotic or psychotropic ones.
sudafed.malaysia: Pseudoephedrine is not named in Malaysia's Traveller's Guide. As a medicine, only registered products may be imported, and you may carry no more than one month's use for one person, set by the dosage label. Keep the dispensing label and original packaging. The Ministry email is pelesenanbpf@moh.gov.my.
sudafed.maldives: Maldives Customs does not say whether pseudoephedrine is controlled. If it is, the page's rule is a valid prescription from a registered medical practitioner. If it is not, it is an ordinary medicine. Narcotics and psychotropic substances are separately listed as prohibited goods.
sudafed.mauritius: Whether pseudoephedrine counts as a controlled medicine in Mauritius is not stated by the Revenue Authority. As an ordinary prescription medicine, carry a legible prescription, keep it in original containers and bring no more than three months' supply. If controlled, approval and a one-month limit apply.
sudafed.mexico: ANAM does not say whether pseudoephedrine is a psychotropic substance. Medicines for personal use are included in the duty-free baggage allowance, and only psychotropic substances need the medical prescription to be shown. The page sets no quantity limit.
sudafed.nepal: For pseudoephedrine in Nepal we found no source we could verify, so no limit is stated here. Rules on cold remedies with pseudoephedrine differ widely between countries. Carry it in the original packaging with the prescription or a doctor's letter, and ask a Nepali embassy before you travel.
sudafed.nigeria: For pseudoephedrine in Nigeria no official traveller rule was found, so no limit is stated. Rules on cold remedies differ widely between countries. Keep it in the original packaging with a prescription or doctor's letter and check with NAFDAC (nafdac.gov.ng) or customs (customs.gov.ng).
sudafed.norway: Norway's NOMA page does not say whether pseudoephedrine is a narcotic medicine. If it is not, up to 3 months' use is allowed from outside the EEA and up to a year from within it, with proof of personal use. If it is, the 30-day rule and red zone apply.
sudafed.philippines: Whether pseudoephedrine counts as a controlled precursor under the Dangerous Drugs Board is not stated in the circular. As an ordinary medicine, the circular allows it without FDA clearance for personal use if the amount matches the prescription with the physician's PRC licence number or foreign equivalent.
sudafed.poland: Whether pseudoephedrine is on Poland's list of narcotic and psychotropic substances is not stated in the rule we could confirm. If it is, you need the pharmaceutical inspectorate's document, issued up to 15 days before the border crossing, valid at most 30 days. If not, it is an ordinary medicine.
sudafed.portugal: Portugal's article does not say whether pseudoephedrine is in any of the controlled tables. If it is, Article 13 of Decree-Law 15/93 limits you to 30 days of treatment with a medical document. If it is not, it is an ordinary medicine. Check with Infarmed.
sudafed.qatar: Qatar's text does not say whether pseudoephedrine is a controlled medicine. If it is, a Ministry of Public Health permit is needed, requested online with a valid prescription, and applied for at least five working days before you travel. Ask the ministry if you are unsure.
sudafed.romania: Whether pseudoephedrine counts as a narcotic or psychotropic substance is not stated by Romanian Customs. If it does, you must declare it in writing when entering from a non-EU state. Wrong or missing declarations can be fined or prosecuted. Ask customs to be sure.
sudafed.russia: Russian customs does not say whether pseudoephedrine counts. Medicines with no narcotic or psychotropic substances may enter without any permit documents; to know whether yours is restricted, check its composition against the Ministry of Health's register, GRLS. If it is restricted, the document and declaration rules apply.
sudafed.saudi-arabia: The SFDA notice does not say whether pseudoephedrine is a controlled drug. If it is, you need a clearance permit from the SFDA Controlled Drugs System, with a prescription, medical report and ID uploaded. If not, it is an ordinary medicine. Ask the SFDA before you fly.
sudafed.serbia: Serbian customs does not say whether pseudoephedrine counts as a controlled psychoactive substance. Ordinary medicines for your own regular therapy up to 15 days need no medical opinion. A bigger supply, for more than 15 days and up to six months, or more than one package of 30 dosage units, needs approval from the ministry.
sudafed.slovakia: Slovakia's filing does not say whether pseudoephedrine is a controlled substance. If it is, a valid medical prescription is needed and the limits are 7 or 30 days depending on the schedule. The filing is from 2007, so ask the Slovak Ministry of Health about the current rule.
sudafed.slovenia: The Slovenian page does not say whether pseudoephedrine counts as an illicit drug. As an ordinary medicine, arrivals from outside the EU may bring up to three weeks for acute conditions, or three weeks at the prescribed dose for chronic ones, with proof of prescription if it needs one.
sudafed.south-africa: SAHPRA's guideline does not say whether pseudoephedrine is scheduled. If it is a scheduled medicine, one month's supply is allowed with a valid prescription and a certificate. SARS's travellers guide allows personal medicines up to three months with a prescription or letter, so the two sources differ.
sudafed.south-korea: The MFDS page does not say whether pseudoephedrine is covered by the narcotic and psychotropic permit rule. If it is, handling approval must be obtained before you enter Korea. Ask the MFDS Narcotics Policy Division on 043-719-2813 before you fly.
sudafed.spain: The AEMPS page does not say whether pseudoephedrine is narcotic or psychotropic. If not, the general rule applies: a quantity matching your treatment, no more than three months, and a prescription or medical report if asked. If it is, request the AEMPS permit first.
sudafed.cambodia: For pseudoephedrine in Cambodia we found no source, so no limit is stated here. Rules on cold remedies differ widely between countries. Keep Sudafed in its original packaging with the prescription or a doctor's letter, and ask a Cambodian embassy before you travel.
sudafed.costa-rica: Costa Rica's rule does not say whether pseudoephedrine is under international control. If it is, one month of treatment may be carried with the prescription and a doctor's clinical summary issued within three months, translated into Spanish. A longer period needs a JVD assessment.
sudafed.cuba: Pseudoephedrine is not named in Cuba's 2022 filing with the INCB, so whether Sudafed is controlled there is not stated. Controlled medicines need a valid prescription, a certificate endorsed by your home health authorities and one from Cuban authorities. Ask the Cuban Ministry of Public Health.
sudafed.sri-lanka: The NMRA page does not say whether pseudoephedrine is in Schedule III. If not, you may carry it without approval for your stay or 90 days, whichever is less. More than 90 days needs the NMRA's prior approval. Intramuscular or intravenous medicines are not permitted.
sudafed.sweden: Swedish Customs does not say whether pseudoephedrine is narcotic. If it is not, other medicines may be brought for personal use up to three months' consumption from outside the EEA or a year's from the EEA, with proof such as a prescription or label.
sudafed.switzerland: Swissmedic does not say whether pseudoephedrine is a narcotic. If it is not, a private individual may import up to one month's supply for personal use, no certificate needed, based on the prescription or leaflet dose. If it is, 30 days with a certificate.
sudafed.taiwan: Taiwan's customs page does not say whether pseudoephedrine is controlled. If not, it is covered by the other prescription or non-prescription limits: 12 bottles per type and 36 in total without a permit. If a medicine is prescription-only in Taiwan but over the counter where you bought it, the non-prescription allowance applies.
sudafed.turkey: Turkey's customs page does not mention pseudoephedrine. As a medication for personal treatment it is allowed in a reasonable quantity for your stay, with a medical report or doctor's prescription to show at customs. In unforeseen circumstances a regional customs directorate may grant one extension of up to six months.
sudafed.hong-kong: Pseudoephedrine is not named in the Hong Kong Drug Office material we read, which sets a written-approval rule for dangerous drugs and carries a 10-working-day processing time. Whether Sudafed counts is not stated. Ask the Drug Office on 2572 2068 and carry the original packaging.
sudafed.china: Pseudoephedrine is not named in the parts of China's 2025 catalogue we read. For medicines in the narcotic and psychotropic categories, Shanghai Customs asks for a prescription, medical records or a diagnosis certificate, declaration at the port, and a reasonable personal quantity. Ask customs whether Sudafed counts.
sudafed.australia: Pseudoephedrine is not named in the Australian traveller's exemption material we read. The general rule is up to three months' supply for yourself or an immediate family member travelling with you, with a prescription or letter from your doctor. Ask the Office of Drug Control whether Sudafed is treated differently.
sudafed.united-kingdom: Pseudoephedrine is not named in the Home Office's Misuse of Drugs guidance we read, which covers Schedule 2 to 4 drugs with a three-month limit and a doctor's letter. Whether Sudafed counts as controlled is not stated. Ask the Home Office licensing unit, and keep the original packaging.

ritalin.japan: Ritalin contains methylphenidate, which Japan's Narcotics Control Department classes as a psychotropic. Tablets up to the limit in the department's quantity table can be carried without a doctor's certificate or permission; injection forms always need one. For more than a one-month supply, the department asks you to contact it by email before you travel. Carry the medicine yourself, as it cannot be shipped or handed to someone else.
ritalin.united-arab-emirates: Ritalin and other methylphenidate medicines are used for ADHD. The UAE list places methylphenidate in Psychotropic Schedule II, so you may bring only what your stay needs, up to three months. Have a medical prescription or an attested report from your health provider ready, and keep the tablets in the pharmacy packaging with your name on the label.
ritalin.thailand: Thailand’s FDA page lists no drug names, so it does not tell you where Ritalin’s methylphenidate sits. The rule has two tiers for psychotropics: up to a 30-day supply with a doctor’s certificate or prescription, and 31 to 90 days with a permit applied for online at least 15 days ahead. The FDA says a complete application is usually answered in about 3 working days.
ritalin.panama: Ritalin’s methylphenidate is not named in Panama’s January 2025 filing to the UN narcotics board. The filing sets the same terms for narcotics and psychotropics: up to 90 days of supply, with the details in article 4 of Resolution 3143 of 2017. Bring a prescription, an endorsed doctor’s certificate, ID and a case summary from your prescriber made no more than three months ago.
ritalin.bahrain: For Ritalin, the rule filed by Bahrain with the UN narcotics board gives a 7-day limit for narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances alike. Documents: a valid prescription, a doctor’s certificate endorsed in your country of residence and a certificate from Bahrain’s health authorities. The regulator to contact is the National Health Regulatory Authority, cunp@nhra.bh.
ritalin.singapore: Methylphenidate, which is in Ritalin and Concerta, is on Appendix A of the Singapore HSA document guide. You need approval first, applied for at least two weeks before arrival. Each medicine should stay in its original container with the pharmacy label showing your name, the medicine and the quantity. Approved medicines need not be declared at customs, but keep the approval email to hand.
ritalin.united-kingdom: Ritalin’s methylphenidate is a Schedule 2 controlled drug in the UK. The Home Office allows up to a three-month supply with no licence, provided it was prescribed and dispensed to you in your country of habitual residence and you carry it on your person. A longer stay does not change the cap: for more than three months you would write to the Home Office licensing unit at least a month before you travel.
ritalin.china: Ritalin’s methylphenidate is a Category I psychotropic in China’s 2025 catalogue. For Category I, Shanghai Customs allows the maximum quantity permitted under a single prescription, and asks for a diagnosis certificate from a medical institution plus your passport. This is tighter than the Category II group, where the prescribed quantity may be extended.
ritalin.australia: For Ritalin, Australia’s Office of Drug Control names methylphenidate as covered by the traveller’s exemption. Your limit is three months’ supply, for you or an immediate family member on the same trip. Have a prescription or a letter from your doctor naming the medicine and dose, pack it in the labelled original container, and declare it to Border Force on arrival.
ritalin.canada: Methylphenidate, in Ritalin, is one of the controlled substances Health Canada lists by name for travellers. You can bring up to a 90-day supply based on the usual daily dose, for yourself or a person you are responsible for who travels with you. It cannot be posted to Canada. The same rules apply whether you enter or leave the country, and you declare it to customs when you arrive.
ritalin.france: ANSM names methylphenidate, the ingredient in Ritalin, among the medicines that are often controlled abroad, and it also mentions ADHD treatments in general. Coming into France you need no attestation, and the ANSM does not issue one for arriving visitors. The original prescription must be with you. If you are leaving France, check the destination’s rules on the INCB website.
ritalin.netherlands: The Dutch government names Ritalin and Concerta, both methylphenidate, as ADHD medication that falls under the Opium Act, on its List I. To bring it into the Netherlands you need an official certificate from the country you leave. Check whether that certificate has to be legalised, ask the authorities there for their requirements, and keep the medicine in its original packaging so you can prove it is for your own use.
ritalin.united-states: Ritalin’s methylphenidate is a prescription drug and, in the US, a controlled substance too. The FDA page says the DEA generally decides on controlled substances for personal import, with the two agencies coordinating when both have a say. So the FDA’s 90-day allowance for foreign nationals does not settle it. Ask the DEA before you fly.
ritalin.ukraine: For Ritalin in Ukraine, the national rule filed with the INCB in March 2024 sets a limit of 50 tablets or 10 ampoules for psychotropic substances, and 10 ampoules for narcotics. You also need a valid prescription, a customs declaration, a passport and, for medicines registered in Ukraine, a copy of the manufacturer’s quality certificate. Customs can be contacted at post@customs.gov.ua.
ritalin.vietnam: Under the Vietnam Customs page, which cites Decree 54/2017, a visitor may carry medicine for their own treatment for up to 7 days if it is a narcotic, or up to 10 days if it is a psychotropic or precursor drug. The count follows the dose written on your prescription. The page does not name methylphenidate, so check how it is classed before you go.
ritalin.germany: BfArM’s page on travelling with narcotic drugs does not name methylphenidate, so Ritalin’s status in Germany is for your doctor or pharmacist to confirm. For narcotics, a traveller coming from another Schengen state needs an Article 75 certificate, valid for up to 30 days. A separate certificate is needed for each prescribed controlled drug, so two medicines mean two certificates.
ritalin.ireland: For Ritalin in Ireland, the Department of Health’s rule is that a visitor from a Schengen country needs an Article 75 certificate if the medicine contains a Schedule II or III controlled drug under the Misuse of Drugs Regulations 2017. The certificate lasts up to 30 days and applies to one drug. Methylphenidate is not named on the page.
ritalin.israel: For Ritalin, the 90-day personal allowance that Israel gives for medicines does not apply if methylphenidate counts as a narcotic or psychotropic substance, because the Ministry of Health excludes those and sets different rules. The Ministry’s page does not name the drug, so confirm with your doctor and check the guidance before travelling.
ritalin.kuwait: For Ritalin, Kuwait’s March 2024 filing to the INCB gives a 30-day limit for psychotropic substances, and allows only those in schedules 2, 3 and 4. It states that narcotic drugs are currently not allowed. Methylphenidate is not named, so confirm its class before you travel. Show the original prescription at Customs. The licensing office’s telephone is 2421000, extension 59568 or 59569.
ritalin.oman: For Ritalin in Oman, the national rule filed with the INCB sets 30 days for narcotics and 30 days for psychotropics. Bring a valid prescription and a medical report from the institution where you are treated, issued no more than six months before. The report must be recent. The Drug Control Department can be reached on 24602177.
ritalin.lebanon: Ritalin in Lebanon: the 2014 filing to the INCB allows 30 days of psychotropic substances and 7 days of narcotics, and methylphenidate is not named. Among the papers asked for are a pharmacy-stamped certified copy of the prescription, an identity document, a medical report explaining the case, and approval from the Department of Narcotics.
ritalin.peru: For Ritalin in Peru, the January 2025 filing to the INCB says psychotropic substances may be brought in the amount of the medical prescription, but narcotic drugs only up to 5 days. Methylphenidate is not named, so check its class. Carry the original prescription for Customs and a doctor’s certificate endorsed by the health authorities of your home country.
ritalin.kenya: Ritalin in Kenya follows the 30-day rule: the national filing allows 30 days for narcotics and 30 days for psychotropic substances. You need a valid medical prescription and must show the original at Customs. For more detail the Pharmacy and Poisons Board lists the telephone +254 709 770 100.
ritalin.seychelles: For Ritalin in Seychelles, the 2013 filing to the INCB gives 90 days for psychotropic substances and 30 days for narcotic drugs; methylphenidate is not named. Documents: a valid prescription, a doctor’s certificate endorsed by the health authorities of your home country and a certificate from the Seychelles health authorities, plus the original prescription at Customs.
ritalin.morocco: For Ritalin in Morocco, the August 2026 INCB filing lists a valid prescription, a doctor’s certificate endorsed by your home health authority, a certificate from the Moroccan health authorities, and a patient’s written request. If the medicine is not sold in Morocco, an authorization of release for consumption is also needed. No day limit is stated. The agency’s Controlled Substances Unit answers on +212 537 68 22 89.
ritalin.luxembourg: For Ritalin in Luxembourg, the national filing of March 2024 requires a copy of the prescription and a doctor’s certificate endorsed by your home health authority, and says the Schengen agreement applies. It states no day or quantity limit. The Health Directorate’s Pharmacy and Medicines Division can be emailed at infostupefiants@ms.etat.lu.
ritalin.malta: For Ritalin in Malta, the 2017 INCB filing requires a valid medical prescription, applies the Schengen agreement, and sets no day or quantity limit. Methylphenidate is not named. The filing’s contact is the Superintendent of Public Health, whose telephone numbers are (356) 23439176 and 25953302.
ritalin.argentina: Methylphenidate is not listed by name on the Argentine page for Mercosur Resolution 66/2000. If Argentina treats it as a psychotropic, you must show a prescription legalised by the health authority with the doctor's name, address, signature and registration. The page says nothing about how long the prescription stays valid, so ask ANMAT before travelling.
ritalin.austria: Methylphenidate is not named on the Austrian ministry page, which speaks of addictive drugs and psychotropic substances in general. Where it applies, a stay beyond 5 days and up to 30 days needs a prescription from your home doctor, ideally on the form in the Addictive Drugs Regulation, and no more than 30 days' supply. For longer stays an Austrian doctor can prescribe, and a letter from your own doctor helps.
ritalin.belgium: Methylphenidate is named directly: Belgium gives ADHD medicines with methylphenidate as an example of a controlled medicine. You need an official document proving the prescription, either a Schengen declaration validated by your home authorities or, from outside Schengen, a valid prescription or government-validated certificate. The cap is 3 months of treatment, and posting it to Belgium is not allowed.
ritalin.brazil: Methylphenidate is not named on the Anvisa baggage page or the Federal Revenue page on prohibitions. Those pages only say that narcotic drugs are prohibited and medicines are restricted, so the position of Ritalin is not stated. Bring your prescription and confirm with Anvisa or customs..
ritalin.bulgaria: Methylphenidate is not named in the Bulgarian customs FAQ. The rule it gives for narcotic medicines is: only for treatment, up to 30 days of treatment, and with a document from the competent authority of the country where it was prescribed. Whether Ritalin sits on the listed groups is not stated, so ask Bulgarian customs before you pack it.
ritalin.chile: The ISP guide does not name Ritalin or methylphenidate. Its criteria apply to every medicine: a prescription or certificate with daily dose and duration of treatment, translated into Spanish if possible, dated, signed and not older than 6 months. The quantity must match that treatment. The guide lists no separate controlled substances.
ritalin.colombia: For methylphenidate, which the article does not name, Colombia's Article 59 allows travellers on listed psychotropic treatment to carry a standard 30-day supply and requires a copy of the prescription on entry. If you remain more than a month and still need it, you must see a Colombian doctor licensed to practise, who issues the new prescription.
ritalin.croatia: Methylphenidate is not named on the Croatian Customs Administration page. For narcotic-containing medicine the limit is 5 days of personal use with documents from a doctor; the page lists 15 days only for addiction substitution therapy or malignant disease. A Croatian resident travelling to Schengen can have 30 days with a form, which does not apply to visitors.
ritalin.cyprus: Methylphenidate is not named in the Cyprus text we could confirm. For visitors carrying small quantities of internationally controlled medicines, the Ministry of Health's Pharmaceutical Services require a permit from the Inspection Department. Its website publishes the application form and traveller guidelines; the rules on amounts and processing time were not readable to us.
ritalin.czechia: Methylphenidate is not named on the Czech customs page, so whether Ritalin needs a permit is not confirmed. For addictive substances the page requires an import permit from the Ministry of Health and sets out exemptions without describing them. The State Institute for Drug Control (SÚKL) handles human medicines; contact it or customs before you travel.
ritalin.denmark: Methylphenidate is not named on the Danish Medicines Agency page, so check which list it is on in the Executive Order on Euphoriant Substances. For lists B to E you may bring a 30-day personal supply with a prescription or Schengen certificate. Illegal imports are referred to the police. Ask dkma@dkma.dk if unsure.
ritalin.dominican-republic: Methylphenidate is not named in the Dominican customs Manual del Viajero. If it counts as controlled or psychotropic, you must show the medical prescription that justifies its use during your stay. The page does not say what the prescription must look like or how long it may be valid, so contact customs or the Ministry of Health.
ritalin.egypt: Methylphenidate is not named in Egypt's customs regulations. Article 73 of Decree 430 of 2021 treats medicine for personal use as duty-free tourist luggage at the discretion of the control authority, and says nothing more about psychotropic medicines. Without a stated rule, bring the prescription and ask Egyptian customs beforehand.
ritalin.estonia: Methylphenidate is not named by Estonian customs, so check whether it counts as psychotropic. If it does, one retail package of up to 30 units comes in without a permit when you carry a prescription copy or doctor's notice. For more, ask the State Agency of Medicines for authorisation in advance; it covers up to 30 days of treatment.
ritalin.ethiopia: The 2023 EFDA guideline does not mention methylphenidate or Ritalin. It says personal-use medical products are cleared at the port by showing a prescription, and that the quantity is verified against that paper. Items suspected to be unauthorised can be quarantined until the authority decides, so confirm with the EFDA before you travel.
ritalin.fiji: Methylphenidate is not named in Fiji's guideline. A person undergoing treatment who enters or transits Fiji may possess a lawfully prescribed controlled drug for no more than one month, under section 11 of the Illicit Drugs Control Act 2004, and must produce evidence of the prescription and supply. A pharmacy label with prescriber and supplier details also counts as evidence.
ritalin.finland: Methylphenidate is not named on Finland's travel page. If it counts as a narcotic, you may bring 30 days' supply from a Schengen country, with a Schengen certificate from a pharmacy, or 14 days from a non-Schengen country. A repeat import of the same product must wait until the earlier supply period has passed.
ritalin.georgia: Methylphenidate is named in Georgia's customs brochure as a substance that cannot be imported without medical documentation. For personal need you may bring a 31-day supply with an English prescription copy approved by the authority where you travel from, the doctor's certificate, and a signed and sealed confirmation from that authority. Passing it to another person is strictly prohibited.
ritalin.greece: Methylphenidate is not named in the Schengen decision Greece uses. It says residents of a Schengen state who need psychotropic substances on prescription may receive a certificate valid for a maximum of 30 days, and doctors may prescribe up to 30 days for travel.
