For visitors from outside Schengen it gives no rule, so ask Greek authorities.
ritalin.hungary: Methylphenidate is not named in Hungary's rule. Psychotropic substances may be carried up to 30 days with an international certificate from your GP, and for 30 to 90 days only with an official certificate from the competent authority of your country. You must show the documents at the customs and police check.
ritalin.iceland: Methylphenidate is not named by the Icelandic Medicines Agency. For psychotropic medicines, 30 days' supply is allowed for non-residents, counted by defined daily dose. You must be able to present a physician's certificate, the original prescription or a pharmacy sticker if customs asks. From outside the EEA, post of such medicines is not allowed.
ritalin.india: Methylphenidate is not named in India's customs guide or the CDSCO notice. The guide lists psychotropic substances among prohibited imports, and the notice gives no separate rule. Do not rely on a prescription alone; ask Indian customs or an Indian mission for a written answer before you travel.
ritalin.indonesia: Methylphenidate is not named in BPOM's leaflet. Psychotropic medicines may be carried with a mandatory doctor's prescription, up to a maximum of 60 days of treatment, and narcotics not at all, under Regulation 28 of 2023. Everything enters through the Special Access Scheme, and customs decides whether to release it fully, partly or not at all.
ritalin.italy: Methylphenidate is not named in the Italian guidance. A medicine with psychotropic substances falls outside Italy's general rule of no specific requirements. From a Schengen country you need an Article 75 certificate, valid for 30 days, issued on prescription. Others should hold a similar certificate, which Italy's Central Narcotics Office has accepted.
ritalin.jamaica: Methylphenidate is not named on the Jamaica pages. A prescription drug needs a special permit from the Ministry of Health, requested with a physician's letter, a prescription copy with strength and quantity for the stay, your flight dates and flight numbers, your address in Jamaica and a contact phone number of the doctor or patient.
ritalin.jordan: Methylphenidate is not named in Jordan's regulation for travellers. For psychotropic substances you need authorisation from the Narcotic and Psychotropic Substances Control Department of the Jordan Food and Drug Administration to carry them in or out, for personal use, up to six months at most and within the manual's quantity.
ritalin.latvia: Methylphenidate is not named by Latvia's State Agency of Medicines. If it is in Schedule II or III, you may bring a course of up to 14 days (II) or 30 days (III) from outside Schengen without a special permit, showing a prescription or copy. From a Schengen country, a certificate from your home authority is needed.
ritalin.lithuania: Methylphenidate is not among the examples on Lithuanian customs' page. The page's rule for narcotic and psychotropic medicines is personal medical use only, original packaging, your name on it and no more than the prescription says. Psychotropics allow up to 30 days. Ask customs whether methylphenidate counts.
ritalin.malaysia: Methylphenidate is not named in Malaysia's guide. For medicines controlled under the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 and the Poisons (Psychotropic Substances) Regulations 1989, bring a valid prescription or doctor's letter in English (or translated) with the medicine name, dose and quantity. The Third Schedule of the Poisons Act 1952 lists psychotropics.
ritalin.maldives: Methylphenidate is not named on the Maldives Customs page. Controlled drugs for personal use need a valid prescription from a registered medical practitioner, while narcotics and psychotropic substances are on the prohibited list. How the two rules fit together is not explained, so confirm with customs.
ritalin.mauritius: Methylphenidate is not named in the Mauritius customs rule. For controlled medicines the Revenue Authority requires approval from the Government Pharmacist, a legible doctor's prescription, original containers and a one-month limit at most. Ask the Ministry of Health and Quality of Life whether Ritalin is controlled.
ritalin.mexico: Methylphenidate is not named by ANAM. The agency says that for psychotropic substances the corresponding medical prescription must be shown, and personal-use medicines are included in the duty-free baggage allowance. Neither rule defines 'personal use' or an amount, so carry the original prescription.
ritalin.nepal: We found no source for Nepal on Ritalin that we could verify. Methylphenidate is controlled in many countries and often needs permission before travel. The page therefore gives only the general advice: carry the prescription and confirm with the Department of Drug Administration (dda.gov.np) or a Nepali embassy.
ritalin.nigeria: We found no official source for Nigeria on Ritalin, so this page gives no limit or permit rule. Methylphenidate is controlled in many countries and often needs permission first. Carry the prescription and confirm with NAFDAC (nafdac.gov.ng) or a Nigerian embassy before you travel.
ritalin.norway: Methylphenidate is not named by NOMA. If it is a narcotic medicine in Norway, you need documentation such as a prescription or medical certificate, you use the red goods-to-declare zone, and visitors without a Norwegian address may bring up to 30 days' use. For more than 30 days, apply to NOMA by the portal or post; email is not accepted.
ritalin.philippines: Methylphenidate is not named in the joint circular. Dangerous drugs and similar substances are left to the Dangerous Drugs Board and PDEA, with no allowance for travellers. Prescription drugs in general come in without FDA clearance if the quantity matches a prescription showing the physician's licence number.
ritalin.poland: Methylphenidate is not named in the Polish text we could confirm. If it is on Poland's list of psychotropic substances, you need a pharmaceutical inspectorate document, one per product, issued within 15 days before you cross the border and valid at most 30 days. A voivodship inspector handles Schengen travel.
ritalin.portugal: Methylphenidate is not named in the part of Decree-Law 15/93 we could confirm. If it is in tables II-B, II-C, III or IV, Article 13 lets you carry it for your own use up to 30 days of treatment, provided you present a medical document justifying the need.
ritalin.qatar: Methylphenidate is not named in what we could read of Qatar's rule. If it is a controlled medicine there, you need a permit from the Ministry of Public Health, applied for online with a valid prescription, at least five working days before travel, approved or rejected within three working days.
ritalin.romania: Methylphenidate is not named on the Romanian Customs page. Medicines with psychotropic substances must be declared in writing when entering Romania from a non-EU state. The page sets no maximum quantity and lists no documents, so carry your prescription and declare it anyway.
ritalin.russia: Methylphenidate is not named by the Federal Customs Service. If it counts as psychotropic, you need medical documents naming the medicine and quantity, in Russian or with a notarised Russian translation, and a written declaration on the passenger customs declaration. Sending it by post is not allowed.
ritalin.saudi-arabia: Methylphenidate is not named in the SFDA notice of 14 August 2025. For psychotropic or narcotic medicines the SFDA requires a clearance permit through its online Controlled Drugs System: create a personal account, enter patient and trip details, and upload the prescription, medical report and ID.
ritalin.serbia: Methylphenidate is not named by Serbian customs. The page says medicines containing controlled psychoactive substances should have ministry approval for personal import, and so should more than one package of up to 30 dosage units. For stays of more than 15 days, up to six months, approval is needed in any case.
ritalin.slovakia: Methylphenidate is not named in the Slovak INCB filing. For psychotropic substances, 7 days are allowed for Schedule II and 30 days for Schedules III and IV of the 1971 Convention, on a valid medical prescription. Further information comes from the Ministry of Health's Department of Pharmacy in Bratislava.
ritalin.slovenia: Methylphenidate is not named on the Slovenian page. If it counts as an illicit drug used as medicine, you need a medical certificate issued or endorsed by the competent authority of your country of permanent residence. The page covers personal use, family members, and one non-family person under authorisation.
ritalin.south-africa: Methylphenidate is not named in the SAHPRA guideline. Regulation 8(1) allows a Schedule 3, 4, 5 or 6 substance for personal use up to one month's supply, with a valid prescription, a prescriber's certificate and your residence particulars recorded at the port of entry. SARS says narcotics and habit-forming drugs are prohibited goods.
ritalin.south-korea: Methylphenidate is not named on the MFDS page. The permit requirement applies to any medicine with a narcotic or psychotropic substance, for Koreans and foreigners alike, and has been in force since 23 October 2009. You can apply online. The page gives no quantity limits.
ritalin.spain: Methylphenidate is not named by AEMPS. If it counts as a psychotropic medicine, you need a permit from the Narcotics and Psychotropics Area to bring it for your own treatment. The page says storage must follow each medicine's specifications, and gives no email or phone for the area.
ritalin.cambodia: We found no source for Cambodia on Ritalin. Methylphenidate is controlled in many countries and often needs advance permission, so this page gives only the general advice: carry the prescription in original packaging and confirm with the Cambodian embassy or health authority before you fly.
ritalin.costa-rica: Methylphenidate is not named in the Costa Rican requirements. For psychotropic medicines under international control, the JVD allows one month of treatment, with documents translated into Spanish: ID copy, prescription, epicrisis no older than three months, invoice if any. More than a month must be assessed by the JVD.
ritalin.cuba: Methylphenidate is named in Cuba's regulation: a maximum of 1 g, for your stay and up to 30 days, with official medical documentation. That means a valid prescription, a doctor's certificate endorsed by the authorities of your country of residence, and a certificate issued by the health authorities of Cuba.
ritalin.sri-lanka: Methylphenidate is not named by the NMRA. If it is listed in Schedule III, it is not permitted. Otherwise you may carry your own medicine without approval, for the length of your stay or 90 days, whichever is less, in its original container or labelled with its name, strength and instructions.
ritalin.sweden: Methylphenidate is not named by Swedish Customs. If it counts as narcotic, you must prove medical purpose and personal use with a prescription, pharmacy label or doctor's certificate, and sometimes also a Schengen certificate. If your medicine complies, use the green or blue lane with nothing to declare.
ritalin.switzerland: Methylphenidate is not named by Swissmedic. If it counts as a narcotic, you may bring up to 30 days of treatment with a certificate for that medicine, ideally in hand luggage and original packaging. For longer stays, a Swiss doctor can prescribe, since importing more than a month is not possible.
ritalin.taiwan: Methylphenidate is not named on Taiwan's customs page. If it is a controlled drug, you may carry up to a 6-month supply with a prescription or supporting document and a TFDA-certified statement. The dosage must not exceed what the prescription states. Exceeding limits means declaring in the red channel.
ritalin.turkey: Methylphenidate is not named on the Turkish page. The page's only medication rule is that personal-treatment medicines are allowed, in a reasonable quantity for your stay, with a medical report or prescription to show at customs. It does not say whether controlled medicines need anything more, so ask Turkish customs.
ritalin.new-zealand: Methylphenidate's status in New Zealand is for Medsafe's classification database to say, which we did not read. If it is a controlled drug, the limit is one month carried in person and declared on the arrival card; if not, three months with a prescription copy or doctor's letter and the original container.
ritalin.hong-kong: Methylphenidate is not among the examples we read in Hong Kong's Drug Office rules, which require written approval for listed dangerous drugs and do not issue import licences for pharmaceuticals sent by post for personal use. Ask the Drug Office, pharmgeneral@dh.gov.hk, whether Ritalin is listed before you travel.

ambien.japan: Ambien contains zolpidem, which Japan's Narcotics Control Department lists as a psychotropic. Amounts within the department's quantity table can be carried without a doctor's certificate or permission, but a larger amount needs both. For more than one month's supply, contact the department by email before you fly. The department says to carry the medicine yourself.
ambien.united-arab-emirates: Ambien is a sleep medicine, and its zolpidem sits in Psychotropic Schedule IV on the UAE list for travellers. The limit is the quantity for your stay or three months, whichever is smaller. The list asks you to carry a medical prescription or an attested medical report. The UAE treats controlled medicines as restricted items, so keep the original packaging.
ambien.singapore: Zolpidem, the ingredient in Ambien, is listed on Appendix A of Singapore’s HSA document guide, which means you need approval before you travel. Send your application at least two weeks before arrival, with medical documents and product photographs. If you only wait in the transit zone or leave it for a layover, the HSA says no approval is needed for controlled substances, but prohibited medicines are not allowed in either case.
ambien.united-kingdom: Ambien’s zolpidem is in Schedule 4 (Part 1) of the UK Misuse of Drugs Regulations. The Home Office policy covers Schedules 2 to 4 (Part 1) together: up to three months’ supply, lawfully prescribed to you where you live, carried on you, needs no licence. Its guidance advises a letter from your doctor naming the medicine, dose, strength and frequency.
ambien.china: China’s 2025 catalogue places zolpidem, the ingredient in Ambien, among Category II psychotropics. Shanghai Customs says the prescribed quantity may be extended where appropriate for this group, and advises travellers to carry prescriptions, medical records or a diagnosis certificate and to declare the medicine to officers at the port. Customs clears it on the principle of personal use and a reasonable quantity.
ambien.australia: Sedatives, the group that includes Ambien’s zolpidem, are listed by the TGA as covered by the traveller’s exemption. Australia lets you bring up to three months’ supply for your own use or for an immediate family member with you. Carry the prescription or a doctor’s letter, keep the dispensing label on the box, and declare the medicine to the Australian Border Force.

xanax.japan: Xanax contains alprazolam, a psychotropic on Japan's list from the Narcotics Control Department. A small supply within the department's quantity table needs no certificate or permission. More than that, or any injection form, needs a doctor's certificate and permission. For over a month's supply, the department asks you to email it first.
xanax.united-arab-emirates: Xanax is prescribed for anxiety and panic disorder. The UAE list shows its alprazolam as Psychotropic Schedule IV, a controlled medicine you may bring only in a limited amount: your stay, to a maximum of three months. Pack the prescription or an attested medical report with it. If your plans are unclear, the health ministry’s personal-use permit service is the place to ask before you fly.
xanax.singapore: Alprazolam, in Xanax, is on Appendix A of Singapore’s HSA list of controlled substances that need approval. Apply at least two weeks before arrival and attach your prescription or doctor’s letter and photos of the packaging. The HSA’s enquiry address is PTM_Enquiry@hsa.gov.sg, but it replies only to questions its published pages do not already answer.
xanax.united-kingdom: Alprazolam, in Xanax, is a Schedule 4 (Part 1) drug in the UK, and the Home Office three-month rule covers it without a licence. Only your own prescription counts: it must have been prescribed and dispensed to you in your country of habitual residence. If your doctor writes a letter, the Home Office wants the prescriber’s signature and professional registration details on it.
xanax.china: Alprazolam, in Xanax, is a Category II psychotropic in China’s 2025 catalogue. Shanghai Customs advises Category II travellers to declare the medicine on arrival and to carry prescriptions, medical records or diagnostic certificates. Customs decides on the spot, on the basis of personal use and a reasonable quantity, so a clear paper trail helps more than a large supply.
xanax.australia: Xanax contains alprazolam, a benzodiazepine, and the Office of Drug Control names that whole group as covered by Australia’s traveller’s exemption. The allowance is three months’ supply for you or an immediate family member on the trip. Documents: a prescription or doctor’s letter with the medicine and dose. Keep the dispensing label on the pack and declare it to Border Force.
xanax.hong-kong: Xanax’s alprazolam is a dangerous drug under Hong Kong’s Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, so even transit passengers need the Drug Office’s written approval. Send it a doctor’s letter with the doctor’s registration number, the clinic’s address, your full name and home address, and the strength and total quantity. After you have all the documents in, processing normally takes 10 working days; keep both papers on you in Hong Kong.

klonopin.japan: Klonopin contains clonazepam, which Japan's Narcotics Control Department lists as a psychotropic. You may carry an amount up to the limit in its quantity table without extra paperwork. Above that limit, you need a doctor's certificate and permission under Japan's narcotics and psychotropics law. The department wants an email before you bring more than a month of supply.
klonopin.united-arab-emirates: Klonopin is used for seizure disorders and panic disorder. In the UAE list its clonazepam is Psychotropic Schedule IV. The allowance is the quantity for your stay, capped at three months, and the document to carry is a prescription or an attested report from your health provider. A longer trip does not raise the cap, so ask your doctor how to cover the rest.
klonopin.singapore: Clonazepam, the active ingredient of Klonopin, is listed on Appendix A of Singapore’s HSA document guide. You need approval before you fly, applied for in English at least two weeks ahead. The HSA wants clear photos showing the product name, active ingredient, strength, directions and dispensed quantity, and keeping the approval email with you is advised for arrival.
klonopin.united-kingdom: Klonopin’s clonazepam is Schedule 4 (Part 1) in the UK. The Home Office allows a personal supply of up to three months without a licence when it has been lawfully prescribed and dispensed to you abroad and you carry it yourself. The Home Office also notes that many controlled drugs are not normally prescribed for more than one month at a time.
klonopin.china: Klonopin’s clonazepam is listed as a Category II psychotropic in China’s 2025 catalogue. For this group Shanghai Customs says the prescribed quantity may be extended where appropriate. Present your prescription, medical records or a diagnosis certificate, and declare the medicine at the port of entry. The final decision is made by customs officers at the border.
klonopin.australia: Klonopin’s clonazepam is a benzodiazepine, and the Office of Drug Control lists benzodiazepines as covered by Australia’s traveller’s exemption. You may bring up to three months’ supply for your own use or for an immediate family member travelling with you. A prescription or doctor’s letter and the original labelled packaging are what to carry, and you declare it on arrival.
klonopin.hong-kong: Clonazepam, in Klonopin, is a listed dangerous drug in Hong Kong. The Drug Office says a visitor must hold written approval from the Department of Health before bringing it, whether staying or in transit. Your own doctor’s letter must carry an original signature. The Drug Office does not issue import licences for pharmaceutical products sent by post for personal use, so carry the medicine yourself.
klonopin.canada: Clonazepam, in Klonopin, is named by Health Canada among the controlled substances you may carry for up to 90 days, based on the usual daily dose. Keep it in the container from your health care provider with the label intact: your name, the prescriber, the medicine, daily dose, form, quantity and strength. Declare it to customs. Do not send it ahead by mail, which Health Canada does not allow.

valium.japan: Valium contains diazepam, a psychotropic on the list kept by Japan's Narcotics Control Department. Amounts within the department's quantity table can travel without permission or a doctor's certificate. A larger amount, or an injection, needs both. Contact the department by email if you plan to carry more than one month's supply.
valium.united-arab-emirates: Valium is prescribed for anxiety, muscle spasm and some seizure conditions. The UAE list shows diazepam as Psychotropic Schedule IV. Travellers may carry the amount for the period of their stay, up to three months, with a prescription or an attested medical report. Controlled medicines are restricted items in the UAE, so keep the packaging intact.
valium.singapore: Diazepam, sold as Valium, is named on Appendix A of Singapore’s HSA document guide, so the answer is approval first, travel second. Apply at least two weeks before arrival with a prescription or doctor’s letter. Do not plan on sharing: the HSA does not allow medicines for another person, except an immediate family member for whom they were prescribed.
valium.united-kingdom: Diazepam, as in Valium, is a Schedule 4 (Part 1) drug under UK law. A traveller can carry up to three months’ supply with no licence, if it was prescribed and dispensed to them in the country where they live. The Home Office suggests carrying a letter from the prescriber that names the medicine, strength, dose and frequency, so you can show you are within the limit.
valium.china: Diazepam, as in Valium, is a Category II psychotropic in China’s 2025 catalogue of psychotropic drugs for medical use. Shanghai Customs’ advice is to declare it proactively at the port and to bring prescriptions, medical records or diagnostic certificates. It adds that customs clears these medicines on the basis of personal use and reasonable quantity.
valium.australia: Diazepam, sold as Valium, is a benzodiazepine, so it comes under the group the Office of Drug Control names in Australia’s traveller’s exemption. Up to three months’ supply is allowed for you or an immediate family member travelling with you. Bring the prescription or a doctor’s letter, leave it in the pharmacy-labelled pack, and declare it to the Australian Border Force.
valium.hong-kong: Diazepam, as in Valium, is one of the examples of a dangerous drug that the Hong Kong Drug Office itself gives. Any visitor, including someone in transit, needs the Department of Health’s written approval first. The application requires a doctor’s certification letter with the full name and medical registration number of the doctor, and a total quantity. Plan for 10 working days of processing.
valium.netherlands: Valium is named by the Dutch government as an anxiety medicine under the Opium Act, where sleeping pills and anxiety drugs sit on List II. It can come into the Netherlands only with an official certificate. The page says to check whether the certificate needs legalising and what the country you leave requires. Carry the tablets in the original packaging and be able to show they are for you.

suboxone.japan: Suboxone contains buprenorphine, which Japan's Narcotics Control Department lists among the psychotropics. A supply within its quantity table can be carried without a doctor's certificate or permission, while injection forms always need them. Past that limit you need a doctor's certificate and permission, and for over a month's supply the department asks you to email it first.
suboxone.united-arab-emirates: Suboxone treats opioid dependence, and its buprenorphine is listed by the UAE as Psychotropic Schedule III. The traveller rule on the list applies: carry the quantity for your stay, at most three months, with a prescription or an attested report from your health provider.
suboxone.singapore: Buprenorphine, the ingredient in Suboxone, appears on Appendix A of the Singapore HSA document guide and needs approval before you travel. Apply in English at least two weeks before you arrive; the approval is valid for the arrival date you state. Keep the approval email and your medical papers ready, since officers at the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority may ask to see them.
suboxone.united-kingdom: Suboxone’s buprenorphine is a Schedule 3 drug in the UK. The Home Office guidance puts Schedule 3 inside its ‘Schedules 2 to 4 (Part 1)’ wording: a supply up to three months, lawfully prescribed and dispensed to you where you live, can be carried in without a licence. Keep it with you rather than sending it ahead, as the guidance speaks of medicines carried on your person.
suboxone.china: Suboxone contains buprenorphine, which China’s 2025 catalogue lists as a Category I psychotropic. You may carry up to the maximum quantity allowed on a single prescription. Shanghai Customs asks for a diagnosis certificate issued by a medical institution and a valid identity document such as your passport. Customs clears it on personal use and reasonable quantity.
suboxone.france: The ANSM list of narcotic-type medicines often controlled when travelling includes high-dose buprenorphine, the form used in some Suboxone-type treatments. Entering France you need no personal transport attestation, and none is issued to arriving travellers. The French authorities require you to carry the original prescription. For French customs matters, the agency points to the douane.gouv.fr website.

codeine.japan: Japan’s Narcotics Control Department lists codeine as a narcotic. A medicine that falls under this rule needs an import certificate before you enter, and you show that certificate to Customs. Check the strength of your product against the rule above first. If a certificate is needed, apply at least 14 days before travel and attach a doctor’s certificate issued within three months that states the specific medical reason.
codeine.united-arab-emirates: Codeine is used for pain and cough, and the UAE list places it in Narcotic Schedule II. Under the UAE’s 2021 federal drug law, importing narcotics outside regulated medical use is a crime. For travellers the list allows the stay’s quantity, to a maximum of three months, with a prescription or an attested medical report.
codeine.thailand: Codeine can fall under Thailand’s narcotics rule, but the FDA page does not name it, so check how it is scheduled before you go. For narcotic drugs in Schedules II or III, a permit is required, applied for online at least 15 days before you arrive or leave, and the supply may not exceed 90 days as prescribed. The permit portal is run by the Thai FDA.
codeine.panama: Panama’s January 2025 filing gives no drug list, so codeine is not named. It does say that substances in Schedule IV of the 1961 UN Convention are prohibited, and that other controlled medicines are allowed for up to 90 days with a prescription, an endorsed doctor’s certificate, ID and a case summary dated within three months.
codeine.bahrain: Bahrain’s February 2024 filing sets 7 days as the limit for narcotics. It asks for a valid prescription, a doctor’s certificate endorsed in your country of residence and a certificate from Bahrain’s health authorities. Questions go to the National Health Regulatory Authority, telephone 17113222.
codeine.singapore: Codeine is among the substances on Appendix A of Singapore’s HSA document guide, so you need approval before you bring it in. Apply at least two weeks before arrival, in English only. A prescription from home is not a substitute for the approval. If the approval is late, the HSA suggests asking a registered Singapore doctor for a local alternative.
codeine.united-kingdom: Codeine is Schedule 2 in the UK, or Schedule 5 for some low-dose compound products, so the answer depends on the product. For the Schedule 2 form, the Home Office allows up to three months’ supply without a licence if it was prescribed and dispensed to you in your country of habitual residence. Carry a letter from your doctor with the medicine, strength, dose and frequency.
codeine.china: China’s 2025 narcotics catalogue lists codeine. For narcotics, Shanghai Customs allows the maximum quantity permitted under a single prescription; travellers need a diagnosis certificate from a medical institution and a valid identity document such as a passport. Customs decides on the basis of personal use and a reasonable quantity.
codeine.australia: In Australia, any medicine containing codeine, whatever the strength, needs a prescription or a letter from your doctor. Within that, the traveller’s exemption allows up to three months’ supply for yourself or an immediate family member travelling with you. Keep it in the original packaging with the dispensing label and declare it to Border Force on arrival.
codeine.france: The ANSM page on travelling with medicines does not name codeine, so whether it counts as a narcotic-type medicine in France is a question for your doctor or pharmacist. What the agency does say is simple: travellers entering France need no transport attestation, and the ANSM issues none. The original of your prescription must travel with you.
codeine.netherlands: The Dutch page puts strong painkillers on List I of the Opium Act, but it does not say whether codeine is among them, and the list is written by active ingredient. That is the pharmacist’s question. If your medicine is on a list, an official certificate is needed to bring it into the Netherlands; otherwise the general rule is that you can prove it is for your own use.
codeine.united-states: For codeine, the question in the United States is who decides. The FDA says the DEA generally rules on whether controlled substances may be imported for personal use, and the two agencies coordinate on products covered by both. Whether your product counts as controlled depends on what it contains, so ask your doctor or pharmacist and check the DEA website before you travel.
codeine.ukraine: Ukraine’s March 2024 filing to the INCB gives no drug list, so codeine’s category is a question for your doctor or pharmacist. The filing asks for a valid prescription, a customs declaration and a passport, and sets quantity limits: 10 ampoules of narcotics, 10 ampoules or 50 tablets of psychotropics, and at most 10 transdermal systems. The State Border Guard Service is at adpsu@dpsu.gov.ua.
codeine.vietnam: Vietnam Customs allows visitors to carry medicines for their own treatment, limited to 7 days’ use for narcotics and 10 days’ use for psychotropics and precursors, worked out from the dose on the prescription. The page is dated 2019 and cites Decree 54/2017. It does not state whether codeine is a narcotic there, so that is a point to confirm.
codeine.germany: BfArM does not name codeine on its page for travellers with narcotic drugs. Whether your product counts is a question for your doctor or pharmacist. If it is a controlled drug, a traveller from another Schengen state needs the Article 75 certificate: valid up to 30 days, authenticated before the journey by the competent health authority of the German Land or an authorised body.
codeine.ireland: Ireland’s Department of Health does not name codeine, but its rule for controlled drugs in Schedule II or III of the Misuse of Drugs Regulations 2017 is clear: visitors from a Schengen country carry an Article 75 certificate, valid up to 30 days, one for each drug. Customs has the final say at the border.
codeine.israel: Israel’s Ministry of Health sets a 90-day limit on personal medicines but excludes narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances from it. Codeine is not named on the page, so whether the general allowance covers your product is a question for your doctor or pharmacist, and the Ministry’s guidance is the place to confirm.
codeine.kuwait: Kuwait’s rule, filed with the INCB in March 2024, says that narcotic drugs are currently not allowed, and codeine is a drug whose class you should confirm with your doctor before you go. Psychotropic substances are allowed for 30 days if they are listed in schedules 2, 3 or 4. The contact is the Narcotic and Psychotropic Licensing Control office at the Ministry of Health.
codeine.oman: Oman’s INCB filing, dated 5 October 2016, allows 30 days of supply whether codeine is treated as a narcotic or as a psychotropic, since both categories have the same limit. You need a valid prescription and a medical report from your treating institution, issued within six months. Contact: Drug Control Department, Ministry of Health.
codeine.lebanon: Lebanon’s filing to the INCB gives only 7 days for narcotic drugs, against 30 for psychotropics. Codeine is not named, so find out which group yours is in. Either way, the filing asks for the approval of the Department of Narcotics at the Ministry of Public Health, whose contact in the filing is narcotics@moph.gov.lb.
codeine.peru: Peru’s rule is very short for narcotics: up to 5 days of supply, with a separate provision for terminally ill travellers in Supreme Decree No. 023-2001-SA. Codeine is not named in the filing, so ask your doctor which group it falls in. Questions go to DIGEMID, the Ministry of Health’s medicines directorate, on (511) 631 4300, extension 6007.
codeine.kenya: Kenya’s INCB filing of March 2024 gives 30 days of supply for narcotic drugs and for psychotropic substances alike, so codeine’s class does not change the limit. Carry a valid medical prescription and present the original at Customs. For questions, write to the Pharmacy and Poisons Board at info@ppb.go.ke.
codeine.seychelles: Seychelles’ filing gives 30 days for narcotic drugs and 90 days for psychotropic substances. Codeine is not named, so ask your doctor which group it belongs to before you plan how much to carry. The Ministry of Health, at P.O. Box 52, Victoria, Mahe, is the contact in the filing. Flunitrazepam is the only prohibited substance listed.
codeine.morocco: Morocco’s filing, dated 10 August 2026, states no day limit for codeine or other controlled medicines. Instead it asks for documents: a prescription, a doctor’s certificate endorsed in your home country, a certificate from Morocco’s health authorities, and the patient’s written request. Contact the Moroccan Agency for Medicines and Health Products at stupefiant@ammps.gov.ma.
codeine.luxembourg: Luxembourg’s INCB filing does not name codeine, and it sets no day or quantity limit. It asks for a copy of the valid medical prescription and a doctor’s certificate endorsed by your home health authority, under the Schengen agreement. The Health Directorate also points to a page on sante.public.lu about travelling with narcotic medicines.
codeine.malta: Malta’s national filing of January 2017 does not name codeine. It asks for a valid medical prescription, notes that the Schengen agreement applies and gives no day or quantity limit. Questions go to the Superintendent of Public Health, St Luke’s Hospital, Gwardamanga, at charmaine.gauci@gov.mt.
codeine.argentina: Codeine is not named on the Argentine government page for Resolution 66/2000, which covers medicines with narcotic or psychotropic substances in general. For a covered medicine you need a prescription legalised by the health authority with the doctor's registration number. The page lists no maximum amount, so confirm with ANMAT whether codeine counts and how much you may carry.
codeine.austria: Austria groups painkillers that contain addictive substances under its Addictive Substances Act, and the health ministry names painkillers as an example. For codeine, a short stay of up to 5 days needs proof of your personal need; a stay up to 30 days needs a prescription from your home doctor. The ministry points to the INCB table for the maximum amounts.
codeine.belgium: Belgium names strong painkillers with morphine as controlled, while codeine is not named in the rule we could confirm. If your codeine medicine is on the Belgian narcotic list, bring proof it was prescribed: a Schengen declaration validated at home for Schengen visitors, or a valid prescription for others. You may carry up to 3 months of treatment and cannot send it by post.
codeine.brazil: For codeine, Brazil's Anvisa baggage page gives no special controlled-drug procedure. The Federal Revenue separates prohibited narcotics from restricted medicines, and the pages do not say which group a codeine tablet falls in. Carry a prescription from your doctor and ask Anvisa or customs to confirm before flying.
codeine.bulgaria: Codeine is not named in the Bulgarian Customs Agency FAQ, which cites Article 58 of the Law on Control of Narcotic Substances and Precursors. If your medicine is on the listed narcotic groups, you may hold it only for treatment, up to 30 days, with a document from the competent authority where it was prescribed. Confirm with customs whether codeine is listed.
codeine.chile: Codeine is not named in the ISP guide, which says Chile has no specific health rule for travellers' medicines and applies one set of criteria to all, controlled ones included. You need a dated, signed prescription under 6 months old with the dose and duration, a quantity that fits the treatment, and the original packaging.
codeine.colombia: Codeine is not named in Colombia's Article 59, but the article sets the rule for medicines on the 1961 and 1971 Convention lists: a standard 30-day treatment for personal use, whatever the substance, and a copy of the prescription shown on arrival. If you stay beyond one month, a doctor licensed in Colombia must issue a new prescription.
codeine.croatia: Croatian customs sets a 5-day limit for medicine containing narcotics, with prescription copies, an illness history or a certified physician's certificate. Codeine is not named on the page. A 15-day limit applies to addiction substitution therapy or treatment of a malignant disease. Check with Croatian customs whether your codeine product counts as a narcotic.
codeine.cyprus: Codeine is not named in the Cyprus rule we could read, which concerns internationally controlled medicines carried in small quantities for your own treatment. For those, the Pharmaceutical Services require a permit from the Inspection Department. Check whether your codeine product is classed as controlled, then request the permit through the published form.
codeine.czechia: Codeine is not named on the Czech Customs Administration page. If your medicine is an addictive preparation, the page says an import permit from the Ministry of Health is normally required, unless a case in sections 20(2) or 21(2) of Act 167/1998 applies. The list of substances is in regulation 463/2013. Ask customs or SÚKL, the State Institute for Drug Control.
codeine.denmark: Codeine is not named on the Danish Medicines Agency page. If your medicine contains a substance from lists B to E, you may carry up to 30 days' personal use, and officials may ask for a prescription or a Schengen certificate as proof. List A substances are not allowed. Euphoriant medicine cannot be posted to Denmark, even bought online from another country.
codeine.dominican-republic: For codeine, the Dominican customs manual gives no list of controlled substances. Its rule for controlled or psychotropic substances is to show the prescription that justifies their use during your stay. Medicines for personal use are otherwise allowed. Customs can be reached at INFO@ADUANAS.GOB.DO or 809-547-7070 for a definite answer.
codeine.egypt: For codeine, Egypt's Decree 430 of 2021 offers only the general medicine line in Article 73: personal-use medicine in a tourist's luggage, at the discretion of the competent control authority. No narcotic-specific procedure, quantity limit or paperwork is listed in the regulations, so the decision is made at the border. Carry your prescription.
codeine.estonia: Codeine is not named in the Estonian customs rule. For narcotic or psychotropic medicine, one retail package of up to 30 units or 25 ml needs only a doctor's notice or prescription copy. Larger amounts, up to 30 days of treatment, need State Agency of Medicines authorisation. Permits for larger medically justified quantities are issued within five working days.
codeine.ethiopia: Codeine is not named in the EFDA guideline, which has no separate rules for narcotic or psychotropic medicines. For personal use, no pre-import permit is required, and the port checks product information and quantity against your prescription. Inspectors may take samples to a laboratory when needed, so carry the original packaging.
codeine.fiji: Codeine is not named in Fiji's March 2024 guideline. Whatever the medicine, a traveller must show evidence of lawful prescription and supply at the border, such as a certified prescription copy or a prescriber's letter. For a controlled drug, section 11 of the Illicit Drugs Control Act 2004 limits possession to one month while entering, leaving or transiting.
codeine.finland: Codeine is not named in Finland's travel page, but narcotic medicines affecting the central nervous system are covered: up to 30 days' supply from a Schengen country, 14 days from a non-Schengen country. Bringing the same narcotic again requires that the time covered by the earlier quantity has already passed. Dangerous combinations of narcotic products may not be imported.
codeine.georgia: Codeine is named in Georgia's customs brochure, together with dihydrocodeine, norcodeine, pholcodine and ethylmorphine and their combined preparations. Importing it needs medical documents: an English prescription copy approved by the authority of the country you come from, the doctor's certificate and a sealed confirmation, for up to a 31-day supply. You may not hand the medicine to anyone else.
codeine.greece: Codeine is not named in the Schengen decision (SCH/Com-ex (94) 28 rev., Article 75) behind Greece's rule. If your medicine counts as a narcotic, a Schengen resident needs a certificate from their national authority, valid for up to 30 days and separate for each drug. Questions go to the Ministry of Health's Medicines Department, Narcotic Drugs Division.
codeine.hungary: For codeine, Hungary's rule depends on how it is classed. Narcotic drugs: up to 3 days' treatment with a GP's international certificate, and 3 to 90 days with an official certificate from the competent authority of your country. Psychotropic substances: up to 30 days with a GP certificate, 30 to 90 days with the official one.
codeine.iceland: Codeine is not named by the Icelandic Medicines Agency. Narcotic and psychotropic medicines may be carried up to a 30-day supply (by defined daily dose) if you are not resident, from inside or outside the EEA. Customs may require a physician's certificate, the original prescription or a pharmacy label. Mail shipments of them are not permitted.
codeine.india: India's customs guide lists narcotic drugs among prohibited imports, and the CDSCO medicines notice says nothing separate for them. Codeine is not named. Whether a prescription codeine medicine for personal use is accepted is not stated, so ask Indian customs or the Indian mission in advance.
codeine.indonesia: Codeine is not named in the BPOM leaflet. Under Regulation 28 of 2023, narcotics are not permitted in passenger belongings and psychotropics need a prescription, up to 60 days of treatment. Customs decides on full release, partial release or detention, sometimes after asking BPOM. Phone (+62 21) 4244691 ext. 3619.
codeine.italy: Codeine is not named in the Italian consulate guidance. If your medicine contains a narcotic, Schengen travellers need an Article 75 certificate valid for 30 days, based on a doctor's prescription. From outside Schengen, Italy's Central Narcotics Office has authorised holders of a similar certificate. Without authorisation customs can confiscate the drug.
codeine.jamaica: For codeine, Jamaica's government pages require a special permit for prescription drugs. You apply to the Ministry of Health Pharmaceutical and Regulatory Division with a physician's letter naming you and the treatment, and a prescription copy showing name, strength and quantity for your length of stay. No maximum amount is stated.
codeine.jordan: Codeine is not named in Jordan's traveller regulation. For narcotic and psychotropic medicines the limit is personal use only, no more than six months, and no more than the quantity set in the international passenger authority manual. Authorisation from the Jordan Food and Drug Administration's Narcotic and Psychotropic Substances Control Department is required.
codeine.latvia: Codeine is not named in the Latvian rule. For medicines with Schedule II or III substances, a certificate from the home authority is needed if you come from a Schengen country; from outside it, up to 14 days (Schedule II) or 30 days (Schedule III) with a prescription copy. These medicines cannot be sent or received by post.
codeine.lithuania: Lithuanian customs lists higher-dose codeine among psychotropic medicines, allowed up to 30 days. You must carry it only for personal medical use, in original packaging, in your own name and not more than your certificate or prescription says. A Schengen state needs a certificate in the set form; other states accept prescription copies.
codeine.malaysia: Codeine is not named in Malaysia's Traveller's Guide, which asks you to declare narcotic-based prescription medicines on arrival. Bring a valid prescription or a letter from your doctor, in English or with a translation, showing the name, dose and quantity. The quantity is limited to what is reasonably needed for one month.
codeine.maldives: Codeine is not named by Maldives Customs, which lists narcotics and psychotropic substances as prohibited and requires a valid prescription from a registered medical practitioner for controlled drugs for personal use. The page gives no quantity limit. Ask customs whether your codeine medicine is covered.
codeine.mauritius: Codeine is not named by the Mauritius Revenue Authority. If it counts as a controlled medicine, you need the Government Pharmacist's approval from the Ministry of Health and Quality of Life, a legible prescription from your doctor, original containers, and a supply of no more than one month.
codeine.mexico: Codeine is not named on Mexico's ANAM baggage page. It says personal medicines are part of the duty-free allowance, and that psychotropic substances require the corresponding medical prescription. The page gives no quantity limit and no prescription format, and narcotics appear on the separate list of banned goods.
codeine.nepal: No official or unofficial source for Nepal on codeine was found that we could rely on, so this page does not give a quantity or a permit rule. Codeine is a controlled medicine in many countries, so carry the original packaging and prescription and confirm the current rule with Nepal's Department of Drug Administration (dda.gov.np).
codeine.nigeria: No official traveller rule for codeine in Nigeria was found, so this page states no limit. Codeine is controlled in many countries, so carry the original packaging and prescription and ask NAFDAC (nafdac.gov.ng) or a Nigerian embassy for the current rule before you fly.
codeine.norway: Codeine is not named on the NOMA page. For narcotic medicines, visitors without a registered Norwegian address may bring up to 30 days' use with a copy of the prescription or a physician's confirmation, and must use the red zone. Someone with a Norwegian address and only foreign documents may bring 7 days.
codeine.philippines: Codeine is not named in the Philippine joint circular of 22 June 2015. If it counts as a dangerous drug, it falls under the Dangerous Drugs Board and PDEA, and no personal allowance is given. Ordinary prescription medicines may be brought without FDA clearance in the quantity on the prescription.
codeine.poland: Codeine is not named in the Polish rule we could confirm. If your medicine contains a substance on Poland's narcotic list, the pharmaceutical inspectorate issues a travel document within 15 days before crossing the border, for no more than 30 days. It applies to carrying the medicine yourself, not to post or courier.
codeine.portugal: Codeine is not named in the Portuguese article we could confirm. Article 13 of Decree-Law 15/93 allows people crossing the Portuguese border to carry controlled substances from the listed tables for their own use, no more than 30 days of treatment, and only with a medical document that justifies the need.
codeine.qatar: Codeine is not named in what we could read of Qatar's rule. A traveller with a controlled medicine needs a Ministry of Public Health permit, applied for through the electronic system with a valid prescription. Decisions come within three working days after all requirements are met; apply at least five working days ahead.
codeine.romania: Codeine is not named by Romanian Customs. A medicine containing narcotic or psychotropic substances must be declared in writing in every case when you enter from a non-EU state. Failing to declare, or declaring wrongly, can lead to a fine or prosecution and the goods being held for confiscation.
codeine.russia: Codeine is not named by Russian customs. Medicines with narcotic or psychotropic substances may enter for personal use only with medical documents that name the medicine and quantity, in Russian or with a notarised translation, and with a written declaration. International post is not allowed for them.
codeine.saudi-arabia: Codeine is not named in the SFDA notice. Controlled drugs with narcotic or psychotropic substances need a clearance permit when you arrive in or leave Saudi Arabia, applied for through the Controlled Drugs System with a prescription, a medical report and proof of identity, with each medicine's trade name, active ingredient, concentration and quantity.
codeine.serbia: Codeine is not named on the Serbian customs page. If your medicine contains controlled psychoactive substances, get approval for personal import from the competent ministry. Regular therapy for up to 15 days needs no medical opinion; for more than 15 days, up to six months, ministry approval is required.
codeine.slovakia: Codeine is not named in Slovakia's filing. For narcotic drugs the limits are 7 days for Schedule I and 30 days for Schedule III of the 1961 Convention, and a valid medical prescription is required. A doctor's certificate endorsed by the health authority of your country of residence is also listed. Schengen rules apply.
codeine.slovenia: Codeine is not named on the Slovenian Financial Administration page. Illicit drugs used as medication are permitted only if needed for treatment and backed by a medical certificate from your country of permanent residence, within the Schengen area. Ordinary prescription medicines need proof of the prescription when customs asks.
codeine.south-africa: Codeine is not named in the SAHPRA guideline. If your medicine is a Schedule 3 to 6 substance, you may enter with one month's supply, a valid prescription and a certificate naming the medicine, quantity and the prescriber with their address. SARS separately lists narcotics and habit-forming drugs as prohibited.
codeine.south-korea: Codeine is not named on the MFDS page. If your medicine contains a narcotic or psychotropic substance, you must obtain handling approval from the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety before entering Korea. The page lists no quantities or documents; an attached guideline covers the application method. English line: +82 43 719 1564.
codeine.spain: Codeine is not named on the AEMPS page. For narcotic or psychotropic medicines you must request a permit from the AEMPS area before entering, and leaving Spain needs a certificate from the same area. For general medicines the limit is three months and you may be asked for a prescription.
codeine.cambodia: No source we could verify covers codeine in Cambodia, so this page gives no quantity or permit rule. Codeine is controlled in many countries. Carry it in the original packaging with the prescription or a doctor's letter, bring only a personal supply, and confirm with a Cambodian embassy.
codeine.costa-rica: Codeine is not named in the JVD text we could confirm. For controlled medicines, one month of treatment may be carried with an ID copy, a prescription, a clinical summary (epicrisis) no more than three months old and the invoice, in Spanish. Schedule III narcotic preparations for personal use can generally be carried without restriction.
codeine.cuba: Cuba's Resolution 104/2022 names codeine among narcotic drugs with a maximum of 12 g, for the length of your stay and a maximum of 30 days. You need a valid prescription, a doctor's certificate endorsed by your country's health authorities and a certificate from Cuban authorities, as official medical documentation.
codeine.sri-lanka: Codeine is not named on the NMRA page. Schedule III medicines are not permitted in Sri Lanka, so check with the NMRA, info@nmra.gov.lk, whether yours is listed. For other medicine, bring the quantity for your stay or 90 days, whichever is less, with your prescription.
codeine.sweden: Codeine is not named on the Swedish Customs page. Narcotic and doping medicines are allowed only for personal medical use, proven by a prescription, label or doctor's certificate. A Schengen certificate may also be required, stating the prescriber, the person and the dosage. Keep the original packaging.
codeine.switzerland: Codeine is not named by Swissmedic, which says some strong painkillers count as narcotics. Narcotic medicines may be imported up to 30 days of treatment, in hand luggage and original packaging with a certificate, one per medicine. Templates exist for Schengen and non-Schengen travel; contact anfragen@swissmedic.ch.
codeine.taiwan: Codeine is not named on the Taiwan customs page. A controlled prescription drug may be carried up to 6 months, with a prescription or supporting document and a statement certified by the TFDA for clearance. Other prescription medicines allow 2 months without a prescription and 6 months with one.
codeine.turkey: Codeine is not named on Turkey's customs page, which has no separate rule for controlled substances. The general rule under Annex-9 is a reasonable quantity of medication for the length of stay, with a medical report or prescription showing it is needed. A medicine can also be sent one month before arrival.
codeine.new-zealand: Whether codeine counts as a controlled drug in New Zealand depends on the product, and we did not read Medsafe's classification database. The two limits to know are three months for prescription medicines that are not controlled, and one month for controlled drugs carried yourself and declared on arrival. Bring a prescription copy or a doctor's letter.
codeine.canada: Codeine is not named in the Health Canada list we read, which covers controlled substances such as amphetamines, methylphenidate, morphine and oxycodone with a 90-day supply limit based on the usual daily dose. If codeine counts, keep it in the original labelled container, declare it on arrival, and never post it to Canada.

oxycontin.japan: OxyContin contains oxycodone, which Japan's Narcotics Control Department lists as a narcotic. Bringing it into Japan needs an import certificate that you show to Customs, whatever the amount. Apply at least 14 days ahead. The doctor's certificate must be dated within three months and state a specific reason; wording like 'for travel' is not accepted.
oxycontin.united-arab-emirates: OxyContin is an extended-release painkiller, and its oxycodone is listed by the UAE as Narcotic Schedule I. The traveller allowance is the quantity for your stay, never beyond three months, and you need a prescription or an attested medical report. The UAE does not allow controlled medicines to be imported freely.
oxycontin.singapore: Oxycodone, the ingredient in OxyContin, is named on Appendix A of Singapore’s HSA document guide, so you need approval before you travel. Your application should include a prescription or doctor’s letter showing your details, the dose, frequency and the total quantity, and photos of the product.
oxycontin.united-kingdom: OxyContin’s oxycodone is Schedule 2 in the UK. Personal imports of up to three months’ supply are allowed without a Home Office licence when the medicine was prescribed and dispensed to you in your country of habitual residence. Carry it on your person with a doctor’s letter that gives the medicine, strength, dose and frequency, and that shows you are within the three-month limit.
oxycontin.china: OxyContin’s oxycodone is on China’s 2025 list of narcotic drugs for medical use. Under Shanghai Customs’ guidance you may carry only up to the maximum quantity allowed on a single prescription. You need a diagnosis certificate from a medical institution and your passport, and clearance rests on personal use and a reasonable quantity.
oxycontin.australia: OxyContin’s oxycodone is named by Australia’s Office of Drug Control as covered by the traveller’s exemption. The rule is three months’ supply at most, for your own use or an immediate family member with you. Carry a prescription or doctor’s letter that names the medicine and dose, and keep the dispensing label on the original pack. Declare it on arrival.
oxycontin.hong-kong: OxyContin’s oxycodone is a dangerous drug in Hong Kong, so approval comes before travel: the Drug Office issues written approval to visitors, including those in transit. The doctor’s letter that supports your application should give the clinic’s name and address, the date, your name and home address, and each medicine’s strength and total quantity. Expect about 10 working days to process it.
oxycontin.canada: Oxycodone, the ingredient in OxyContin, is named by Health Canada as a controlled substance travellers can carry for up to 90 days. The container must come from a health care provider and carry a label with the prescriber’s name, the medicine, the daily dose, and the form, quantity and strength. Customs must be told when you arrive. For longer stays, the Exemptions Section at exemption@hc-sc.gc.ca is the contact.
oxycontin.france: Oxycodone appears in ANSM’s examples of narcotic-type medicines that are often controlled when travelling. For a traveller arriving in France no personal transport attestation is required by the health authorities. Carry the original prescription, which is mandatory. The attestation matters for the way out, when you travel from France to a non-Schengen country and apply to the ANSM at least ten days before departure.

morphine.japan: Morphine is a narcotic under the list of Japan's Narcotics Control Department. You need an import certificate before you enter Japan, and Customs asks to see it. No amount is exempt. If you will take leftover medicine out of Japan again, an export application is needed as well, and the reason should say you are returning home or going to another country.
morphine.united-arab-emirates: Morphine is a strong pain medicine, and the UAE list gives it as Narcotic Schedule I. A traveller may carry the amount for the stay, up to three months, together with a prescription or an attested report from the health provider. Federal Law by Decree No. 30 of 2021 treats importing narcotics outside medical use as a crime.
morphine.singapore: Morphine is on Appendix A of Singapore’s HSA document guide, the list of controlled substances that need approval. Apply at least two weeks before arrival with your medical documents and clear photographs of the product. Approvals are tied to your stated arrival date, so a changed travel plan means a new application. The medicine should travel in its original, pharmacy-labelled container.
morphine.united-kingdom: Morphine is a Schedule 2 controlled drug under the UK’s Misuse of Drugs Regulations 2001. Up to three months’ supply, lawfully prescribed and dispensed to you where you live and carried on you, needs no licence. For more than three months the Home Office treats it as an exceptional case, asks you to email its licensing team a month before travel, and says the cost of UK treatment alone is unlikely to qualify.
morphine.china: Morphine is in China’s 2025 catalogue of narcotic drugs for medical use. A traveller may carry up to the maximum quantity permitted under a single prescription, with a diagnosis certificate issued by a medical institution and a passport or other valid identity document. Customs clears it on personal use and reasonable quantity.
morphine.australia: Australia’s Office of Drug Control names morphine as covered by the traveller’s exemption. You may bring up to three months’ supply, for yourself or an immediate family member travelling with you, with a prescription or a letter from your doctor naming the medicine and dose. Declare it to Australian Border Force and keep the dispensing label on the pack.
morphine.hong-kong: Morphine is a dangerous drug in Hong Kong, so a visitor needs prior written approval from the Department of Health’s Drug Office. Include a doctor’s letter showing the medicine’s name, dosage form, strength and total quantity, with the doctor’s original signature and registration number. Carry the letter and the approval at entry and for your whole stay. Contact the Drug Office on pharmgeneral@dh.gov.hk.
morphine.canada: Health Canada lists morphine among the controlled substances you may bring into Canada, up to a 90-day supply based on the usual daily dose. A practitioner such as a doctor, dentist or nurse practitioner must have prescribed it. The medicine may be for you or for a person you are responsible for who travels with you. Declare it on arrival; a doctor’s note is optional.
morphine.france: France’s medicines agency ANSM names morphine among the narcotic-type medicines that are often controlled when travelling. Entering France, you need no transport certificate, and the ANSM does not issue one for arriving travellers; what you must carry is the original of your prescription. The rule is different when you leave: for non-Schengen trips the ANSM issues a certificate covering at most 28 days of treatment.

ativan.united-arab-emirates: Ativan is taken for anxiety, and the UAE list gives its lorazepam as Psychotropic Schedule IV. Travellers may carry the amount needed for their stay, never more than three months’ worth. A prescription or an attested report from your health provider is the document the list asks for. The UAE health ministry also runs an online service for personal-use import permits, linked from the government portal.
ativan.singapore: Lorazepam, sold as Ativan, is named on Appendix A of the Singapore HSA document guide, so it needs approval before you travel. Apply in English at least two weeks before arrival, with medical papers and photos of the product. If the approval does not come in time, the HSA suggests seeing a Singapore Medical Council-registered doctor for local advice and a substitute.
ativan.united-kingdom: Ativan’s lorazepam sits in Schedule 4 (Part 1) of the Misuse of Drugs Regulations 2001. For travellers the Home Office rule is simple: up to three months, prescribed and dispensed to you in your home country, carried on your person, and no licence. It recommends a letter that shows from your travel dates and quantities that you are not carrying more than three months’ worth.
ativan.china: For Ativan, Shanghai Customs’ guidance on psychotropic medicines applies, and China’s 2025 catalogue files lorazepam as a Category II psychotropic. Declare it proactively to customs officers at the port. The guidance does not give a number of tablets; it speaks of personal use and a reasonable quantity, so carry the prescription or a diagnosis certificate that shows how much you need.
ativan.japan: Ativan’s lorazepam is on Japan’s list of psychotropics kept by the Narcotics Control Department, and the quantity table sets a total of 90 mg that you can carry with no permission and no doctor’s certificate. Past that amount, or for an injection, a doctor’s certificate naming the illness and the reason is needed. If you carry more than a month’s supply, email the ministry’s pharmaceutical inspectors at yakkan@mhlw.go.jp before you travel.
ativan.australia: The Office of Drug Control names benzodiazepines as covered by Australia’s traveller’s exemption, and Ativan’s lorazepam is a benzodiazepine. You can bring three months’ supply for yourself or an immediate family member travelling with you. Take a prescription or a doctor’s letter naming the medicine and dose, and declare it at the border. Carrying it for anyone else is against the law.
ativan.hong-kong: For Ativan, a visitor to Hong Kong needs prior written approval from the Department of Health’s Drug Office, because lorazepam is listed as a dangerous drug. The application needs a letter from the doctor who prescribes it, showing the medicine’s name, dosage form, strength and total quantity, signed in original by the doctor. The Drug Office states a normal processing time of 10 working days.
ativan.canada: Lorazepam, sold as Ativan, appears in Health Canada’s own list of controlled substances that travellers may carry. The allowance is up to 90 days of supply, in the container you got from your practitioner, with a label showing the drug identification number if there is one. If you will stay longer than 90 days, Health Canada asks you to email its Exemptions Section at exemption@hc-sc.gc.ca with a brief description.

tramadol.united-arab-emirates: Tramadol is a pain medicine. The UAE list files it simply as a controlled drug (CD), not under a numbered schedule. The rule for travellers is the same one used across the list: the quantity for your stay, up to three months, with a prescription or an attested medical report. If your doctor prescribed more than that, ask for a smaller supply for the trip.
tramadol.thailand: Thailand’s FDA page gives no list of drugs, so it does not state which category tramadol is in. What it does set is the structure: narcotics in Schedule II or III need a permit and at most a 90-day supply, while psychotropics are allowed for 30 days with a prescription or doctor’s certificate. Longer psychotropic supplies, up to 90 days, need a permit too.
tramadol.panama: Tramadol is not named in Panama’s January 2025 filing to the UN narcotics board, which describes narcotics and psychotropics in general terms. The limit it gives is 90 days, and the papers depend on the quantity: a valid prescription, a doctor’s certificate endorsed by your home health authority, ID, and a case summary from the prescriber no older than three months.
tramadol.bahrain: Bahrain’s filing to the UN narcotics board allows a supply of 7 days for narcotic drugs and 7 days for psychotropic substances, and does not name tramadol. Documents required: a valid prescription, a doctor’s certificate endorsed by your home health authority, and a certificate from Bahrain’s health authorities. Contact: cunp@nhra.bh.
tramadol.singapore: Tramadol does not appear on Appendix A of Singapore’s HSA document guide, the list that needs approval. Without it, the HSA allows up to three months’ supply if you carry a copy of a valid prescription or doctor’s letter from your country of residence. Quantities above three months are not allowed, and the medicine should be in its original container, labelled by the pharmacy.
tramadol.united-kingdom: Tramadol is a Schedule 3 drug in the UK, and the Home Office rule that applies is the three-month one: lawfully prescribed and dispensed to you in your home country, carried on you, no licence. If you would need more than three months, the Home Office expects you to email its licensing unit at dflu.ie@homeoffice.gov.uk a month before you travel.
tramadol.china: Tramadol is a Category II psychotropic in China’s 2025 catalogue. Shanghai Customs advises declaring Category II medicines to officers at the port and carrying prescriptions, medical records or a diagnosis certificate. Clearance is based on personal use and a reasonable quantity, and the officer on site has the last word.
tramadol.japan: Japan’s narcotics office says tramadol is not a narcotic, so it falls under the ordinary prescription rule for personal medicines. A supply of up to one month for your own use needs no special procedure. For more, you apply online for an Import Confirmation before you travel and carry a prescription or doctor’s note plus a flight document. Keep it in the original packaging.
tramadol.france: Tramadol is not named in the ANSM’s examples of controlled medicines for travellers, so the card leaves the classification open. For anyone entering France the ANSM’s statement is that no personal transport attestation is required and that none is issued. Your original prescription is mandatory. If you later leave France for another country, check that country’s rules on the INCB website.
tramadol.netherlands: The Dutch Opium Act lists cover strong painkillers, sleeping pills and anxiety drugs, but the government page does not name tramadol. Ask your pharmacist to check the active ingredient against the lists. If it is listed, you need an official certificate to enter the Netherlands, and the departure country’s authorities can tell you how to get one.
tramadol.united-states: The FDA’s personal-importation page does not name tramadol. It says the DEA generally decides whether controlled substances can be imported for personal use, with the FDA coordinating on products under both agencies. If your doctor or pharmacist tells you tramadol is controlled where you live, treat the DEA as the authority to ask before you travel.
tramadol.ukraine: Tramadol is not named in Ukraine’s 2024 filing to the UN narcotics board. If it counts as a psychotropic there, the limit is 50 tablets or 10 ampoules; as a narcotic, 10 ampoules. Bring the prescription, a customs declaration and your passport. For details, the State Customs Service of Ukraine lists the telephone +38 (044) 247-27-24 in the filing.
tramadol.vietnam: For tramadol, Vietnam’s Customs page gives the general rule: your own treatment only, no more than 7 days’ use if it is a narcotic or 10 days’ use if it is a psychotropic or precursor, according to the prescribed dose. The page cites Decree 54/2017 and names no drugs, so ask your doctor or pharmacist which group tramadol is in.
tramadol.germany: Tramadol is not mentioned on BfArM’s travel page, which says only that narcotic drugs listed in Germany need a certificate when you travel within the Schengen area. The certificate lasts up to 30 days and covers one drug. Patients may carry quantities appropriate for the length of the journey, and no fixed figure is given by BfArM.
tramadol.ireland: The Department of Health’s page on travelling into Ireland does not mention tramadol, so check with your doctor whether it is a Schedule II or III controlled drug. If it is, a visitor from a Schengen country needs an Article 75 certificate, which is valid for 30 days and covers a single drug. Visitors from outside Schengen follow the three-month rule.
tramadol.israel: Tramadol is not named on Israel’s Ministry of Health page. The page says only that narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances are excluded from the general 90-day allowance and have different rules. Ask your doctor or pharmacist how tramadol is classed, and read the Ministry’s guidance before you go.
tramadol.kuwait: Tramadol is not named in Kuwait’s 2024 filing to the UN narcotics board. The filing allows travellers psychotropic substances from schedules 2, 3 and 4 for up to 30 days, and says narcotic drugs are currently not allowed. Ask your doctor which group applies. The Ministry of Health’s licensing office can be emailed at sara.almaqseed@moh.gov.kw.
tramadol.oman: Tramadol is not named in Oman’s INCB filing. The filing sets a 30-day limit for both narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances and requires a prescription plus a medical report from the institution where you are treated, not older than six months. The Drug Control Department’s email is mohd.hamdan@moh.gov.om.
tramadol.lebanon: Tramadol is not named in Lebanon’s 2014 filing. The limits it gives are 7 days for narcotic drugs and 30 days for psychotropic substances. The documents include a certified copy of the prescription with the stamp of the pharmacy, an identity document, a medical report explaining the case and the approval of the Ministry of Public Health’s Department of Narcotics.
tramadol.peru: Tramadol is not named in Peru’s 2025 INCB filing. For psychotropic substances, the traveller’s allowance follows the quantity in the medical prescription; for narcotic drugs it is 5 days. The filing prohibits everything on Lists I-A and I-B of annex 2 of Supreme Decree No. 023-2001-SA. Show the original prescription at Customs.
tramadol.kenya: Tramadol is not named in Kenya’s 2024 filing to the UN narcotics board. The limit it gives is 30 days for narcotics and 30 days for psychotropics, with a valid prescription and the original shown at Customs. The Pharmacy and Poisons Board, at Lenana Road in Nairobi, is the national authority named in the filing.
tramadol.seychelles: Tramadol is not named in the Seychelles filing of December 2013. The limits it gives are 30 days for narcotics and 90 days for psychotropics. You need a valid prescription, a doctor’s certificate endorsed by your home health authority and a certificate from Seychelles, and you show the original prescription at Customs.
tramadol.morocco: Tramadol is not named in Morocco’s 2026 filing to the INCB, and the filing gives no day or quantity limit. What it does require is a prescription, a doctor’s certificate endorsed by your home health authority, a certificate from Moroccan health authorities and a written request from the patient, plus a certificate for transport if one applies.
tramadol.luxembourg: Tramadol is not named in Luxembourg’s 2024 filing to the UN narcotics board. For controlled medicines the filing asks for a copy of the prescription and an endorsed doctor’s certificate, applies the Schengen agreement and gives no day limit. The Pharmacy and Medicines Division’s telephone number is +352 247-75567.
tramadol.malta: Tramadol is not named in Malta’s 2017 filing to the UN narcotics board. For controlled medicines the filing requires a valid prescription, applies the Schengen agreement and states no day limit. The contact is the Superintendent of Public Health, whose office fax is (356) 25953304.
tramadol.argentina: The Argentine page on Resolution 66/2000 does not mention tramadol. A medicine that falls under it needs a legalised prescription authorised by the health authority, and a transit passenger shows a legal document with the same details to health or police staff at the airport or border. No amounts are given, so confirm with ANMAT.
tramadol.austria: Austria's ministry gives antidepressants and painkillers as examples of medicines that can contain addictive or psychotropic substances, but it does not name tramadol. If yours counts, the limit is 30 days' needs, backed by a prescription from your home doctor for stays over 5 days. Without a prescription it is not allowed for 5 to 30 days. Check the INCB table the page links to.
tramadol.belgium: Belgium's agency gives strong painkillers as an example of controlled medicines but does not name tramadol in the rule we could confirm. If tramadol is on the Belgian list, bring a Schengen declaration validated by your home authorities, or from outside Schengen a prescription or government-validated certificate, for no more than 3 months. It cannot be posted to Belgium.
tramadol.brazil: Tramadol is not named on Brazil's Anvisa baggage page, which has no separate controlled-substance rule, and customs only lists narcotics as prohibited and medicines as restricted. A strong painkiller can be questioned, so carry your prescription and ask Anvisa how Brazil classes it. The official pages do not give an amount limit.
tramadol.bulgaria: Tramadol is not named in the Bulgarian customs FAQ. The article it cites lets foreign visitors and transit passengers hold medicines containing listed narcotic substances for treatment only, up to 30 days, with a document issued where the treatment was prescribed. Ask the Customs Agency whether tramadol is on the list.
tramadol.chile: Tramadol is not listed by name in the ISP guide, which gives the same criteria for every medicine a traveller carries: a signed, dated prescription under 6 months old, showing the daily dose and the duration of treatment, a quantity that fits it, and the original packaging. Customs counts up to six months of treatment as reasonable.
tramadol.colombia: Tramadol is not named in Colombia's Article 59. If a medicine you carry is on the listed narcotic or psychotropic schedules, the limit is a standard 30-day treatment and you must show the prescription copy. If another country asks for an extra certificate when you leave, Colombia's narcotics fund or a departmental health office can issue it from the clinical history summary.
tramadol.croatia: Tramadol is not named on the Croatian customs page, which draws one line between medicine containing narcotics (up to 5 days, with prescription copies or a certified physician's certificate) and other medicines (up to one month). The page gives no contact for medicine questions, only a general contacts page on carina.gov.hr.
tramadol.cyprus: Tramadol is not named in what we could read of the Cyprus rule. The Pharmaceutical Services require a permit from the Inspection Department for small quantities of internationally controlled medicines for your own treatment, and publish a form and guidelines for travellers. Confirm whether tramadol needs it.
tramadol.czechia: Tramadol is not named on the Czech Customs Administration page. For narcotic substances and preparations it requires a Ministry of Health import permit, plus an origin-country export permit if required, apart from the cases in sections 20(2) and 21(2) of Act 167/1998. Check with the State Institute for Drug Control whether tramadol is on the list.
tramadol.denmark: Tramadol is not named on the Danish Medicines Agency page. If it is on one of the euphoriant lists B to E, you may enter with up to 30 days' personal use and may be asked to show a prescription or a Schengen certificate. Sending such medicine by post is not allowed whatever the sending country. Check the agency's consolidated list.
tramadol.dominican-republic: Tramadol is not named in the Dominican customs manual. The rule it gives for controlled or psychotropic substances is a prescription that justifies their use during your stay. The manual does not define 'personal use' or give a limit, so ask the Dirección General de Aduanas by email at INFO@ADUANAS.GOB.DO.
