Whether a given CBD oil counts depends on which part of the plant it comes from, so ask the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare before you pack it. Importing cannabis can carry up to 7 years in prison.
cbd-oil.australia: The TGA says cannabis and goods containing it cannot come into Australia by post or courier for personal use. Under the traveller’s exemption you can carry it yourself, but only if it is needed for your treatment, prescribed by a medical practitioner and dispensed to you under that prescription, up to three months’ supply. Officers may ask for evidence, and CBD bought abroad outside a prescription may not qualify.
cbd-oil.hong-kong: Hong Kong made cannabidiol a dangerous drug on 1 February 2023, and the government tells travellers not to bring CBD or products containing it into the city. Importing it can bring up to life imprisonment and a fine of HK$5 million. Simple possession can mean up to 7 years in prison and a HK$1 million fine.
cbd-oil.new-zealand: Health NZ treats CBD products as prescription medicines, and Medsafe says medicinal cannabis products, including CBD, cannot be imported for personal use by mail. Carrying one yourself is allowed only if it was prescribed to you, with a copy of the prescription or a letter from the prescriber, in its original labelled container, declared on the arrival card. The limit is three months of a CBD product.
cbd-oil.canada: The Canada Border Services Agency says bringing cannabis across the border in any form, including oils with THC or CBD, without a permit or exemption authorized by Health Canada is a serious criminal offence. The amount does not matter, and a medical document for cannabis does not change it. If you enter with cannabis, you must declare it. Only Health Canada can issue permits or exemptions, in very limited cases.
cbd-oil.france: CBD oil is not named on the ANSM page about travelling with medicines. The agency’s statement for arrivals is general: no personal transport attestation is required to enter France, and the ANSM does not issue one. You must carry the original of your prescription. Ask your doctor or pharmacist how cannabidiol is classed in France, and check French customs rules.
cbd-oil.netherlands: The Dutch government lists medicinal cannabis among the medicines under the Opium Act, but it does not say how CBD oil is treated. Opium Act medicines need an official certificate to enter the Netherlands. Because the page gives no ruling on CBD oil, ask your pharmacist whether your product counts, and check the departure country’s rules too.
cbd-oil.united-states: The FDA page on personal importation does not mention CBD. It says the FDA generally does not allow individuals to import drugs for personal use, with narrow exceptions, and that the DEA generally decides on controlled substances. It may refuse a product on an import alert, one that looks meant for sale, or one that looks like health fraud. Ask the DEA and FDA before you pack CBD oil.
cbd-oil.ukraine: CBD oil does not appear in Ukraine’s March 2024 filing to the UN narcotics board. The filing sets documents (a prescription, a customs declaration, a passport) and limits for narcotics and psychotropics, up to 10 ampoules or 50 tablets. Since CBD is not named, ask the Ministry of Health of Ukraine (moz@moz.gov.ua) whether your product is covered.
cbd-oil.vietnam: Vietnam Customs says visitors may bring medicines for their own treatment, with limits of 7 days for narcotics and 10 days for psychotropics and precursors, based on the prescription. The page, dated 2019, does not mention CBD oil. Because the answer is open, carry a prescription if you have one, and ask the Vietnamese authorities before you travel.
cbd-oil.germany: BfArM’s travel page for narcotic drugs does not mention cannabis or CBD. The page says only that drugs listed in Annex III of the Act on the Trade in Narcotic Drugs may be prescribed, and that a Schengen certificate (Article 75, 30 days, one per drug) is needed for those. Ask your doctor or pharmacist whether your CBD product is covered.
cbd-oil.ireland: Ireland’s Department of Health says prescribed cannabis-based products are not permitted for visitors. That is the line to know for CBD oil. For other controlled drugs in Schedule II or III of the Misuse of Drugs Regulations 2017, Schengen visitors need an Article 75 certificate valid for up to 30 days. Customs has the final say.
cbd-oil.israel: CBD oil is not named on Israel’s Ministry of Health page about carrying medication. The Ministry excludes narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances from its general 90-day allowance and says they have different rules; it adds that supplements sold over the counter elsewhere may count as medicines needing authorization in Israel. Check with the Ministry first.
cbd-oil.kuwait: CBD oil is not named in Kuwait’s March 2024 filing to the UN narcotics board, which allows only psychotropic substances in schedules 2, 3 and 4, for 30 days, and says narcotic drugs are currently not allowed. Because the answer is open, contact the Narcotic and Psychotropic Licensing Control office at the Ministry of Health before you carry it.
cbd-oil.oman: Oman’s INCB filing does not mention CBD oil. For controlled medicines it allows 30 days of supply, with a valid prescription and a medical report from the treating institution issued within six months. Because CBD is not named, ask the Drug Control Department at the Ministry of Health, on 24602177, before you bring it.
cbd-oil.lebanon: CBD oil is not mentioned in Lebanon’s filing to the UN narcotics board. The filing’s limits are 7 days for narcotic drugs and 30 days for psychotropics, and it asks for approval from the Department of Narcotics at the Ministry of Public Health. Because CBD is not named, ask that department, on +9611615745, before you travel.
cbd-oil.peru: CBD oil is not named in Peru’s January 2025 filing. The filing prohibits all substances on Lists I-A and I-B of annex 2 of Supreme Decree No. 023-2001-SA and limits narcotic drugs to 5 days. Because the answer for CBD is open, contact DIGEMID at the Ministry of Health (rpahuara@minsa.gob.pe) before you travel.
cbd-oil.kenya: CBD oil is not mentioned in Kenya’s March 2024 filing. For controlled medicines, the filing gives 30 days of supply and asks for a valid prescription with the original shown at Customs. Because CBD is not named, ask the Pharmacy and Poisons Board (admin@ppb.go.ke) before you bring it.
cbd-oil.seychelles: CBD oil is not named in Seychelles’ filing to the UN narcotics board. The only substance it lists as prohibited is flunitrazepam, and the limits are 30 days for narcotics and 90 days for psychotropics. Since the answer for CBD is open, contact the Ministry of Health on (248) 438 8000 before you travel.
cbd-oil.morocco: CBD oil is not named in Morocco’s August 2026 filing. The filing sets no day limit and asks for a prescription, endorsed doctor’s certificate, a certificate from Moroccan health authorities and a patient’s written request, plus an authorization of release for consumption for medicines not sold in Morocco. Contact the Moroccan Agency for Medicines and Health Products before you pack it.
cbd-oil.luxembourg: CBD oil is not named in Luxembourg’s March 2024 filing. The filing asks for a copy of the prescription and an endorsed doctor’s certificate for controlled medicines, applies the Schengen agreement and states no day or quantity limit. Since the answer for CBD is open, ask the Health Directorate’s Pharmacy and Medicines Division (secretariatdpm@ms.etat.lu).
cbd-oil.malta: CBD oil is not named in Malta’s January 2017 filing to the INCB. It asks for a valid medical prescription for controlled medicines and says the Schengen agreement applies, with no day limit. Because the filing is old and silent on CBD, ask the Superintendent of Public Health (victor.p.pace@gov.mt) before you bring it.
cbd-oil.argentina: The Argentine page on travelling with narcotics and psychotropics does not mention cannabidiol or CBD oil at all. It only sets the paperwork for medicines that are covered: a legalised, health-authority-authorised prescription with your details, the active ingredient, concentration, form and dose. Whether CBD oil is covered is not stated, so check with ANMAT before packing it.
cbd-oil.austria: The Austrian health ministry page does not mention CBD oil. If it is sold to you as a medicine containing an addictive substance, the strict rules apply: a stay of up to 5 days needs only proof of personal need, while 5 to 30 days needs a prescription from your home doctor and a supply of no more than 30 days. Ask the ministry via its contact section if unsure.
cbd-oil.belgium: CBD oil is not among the examples Belgium's agency gives (morphine painkillers, methylphenidate, sleeping pills, methadone, buprenorphine), so its status is not confirmed here. If a CBD product counts as a narcotic or psychotropic, you need a Schengen declaration or a prescription, three months at most, and you may not post it to Belgium. Check with the agency, FAMHP.
cbd-oil.brazil: CBD oil is not mentioned on Brazil's Anvisa baggage page or in the Federal Revenue list of prohibited and restricted goods we read. Customs lists narcotic drugs as prohibited and medicines as restricted, so a CBD product could fall under either depending on what it contains. Check with Anvisa before you bring it and carry the prescription.
cbd-oil.bulgaria: Bulgaria's customs FAQ says tetrahydrocannabinols are not allowed in medicines, which matters for CBD oil because some products contain traces of THC. CBD itself is not named. A medicine with narcotic substances may be held for treatment up to 30 days with a document from the prescribing country. Check the exact THC content on the label.
cbd-oil.chile: The ISP guide to medicines in luggage does not mention CBD oil. For any medicine it asks for a prescription or certificate with the daily dose and length of treatment, ideally in Spanish, dated, signed and under 6 months old. Unlabelled liquids are a problem in Chile, so only carry a labelled, original CBD product.
cbd-oil.colombia: Colombia's Article 59 does not mention CBD oil. It applies only to medicines with narcotics from the 1961 Convention Lists I and II or psychotropics from the 1971 Lists II to IV, and allows a standard 30-day treatment for personal use with a copy of the prescription. Cannabidiol is not named, so confirm whether your product is covered.
cbd-oil.croatia: CBD oil is not named on Croatia's customs page on medicine and narcotics. A medicine that contains narcotics can be brought in only for up to 5 days, with documents such as prescription copies or a certified physician's certificate; other medicines can cover up to one month if approved in the manufacturer's country. Ask customs which group your product falls in.
cbd-oil.cyprus: The Cyprus health ministry text we could confirm does not mention CBD oil. It says only that visitors who bring small amounts of internationally controlled medicines need a permit issued by the Inspection Department, with a form and guidelines on its website. Ask the Pharmaceutical Services whether your CBD product counts as controlled.
cbd-oil.czechia: CBD oil is not named on the Czech customs page. Where a product counts as an addictive substance or preparation, the page requires a Ministry of Health import permit and, if the origin country demands one, its export permit. Which products are covered is set by regulation 463/2013; ask customs at podatelna_generalnireditelstvicel@celnisprava.gov.cz.
cbd-oil.denmark: CBD oil is not named on the Danish Medicines Agency page. It says private persons may hold euphoriant substances in Denmark only when prescribed for treatment, with a prescription kept on entry and during the stay. Look the substance up in the Executive Order's schedules to see its list; list A is banned and the rest are limited to 30 days.
cbd-oil.dominican-republic: CBD oil is not named in the Dominican customs Manual del Viajero. The manual says personal-use medicines are allowed, and that controlled or psychotropic substances need the prescription that justifies their use during your stay. Customs also lists drugs as restricted, so ask the Dirección General de Aduanas, tel. 809-547-7070, before packing it.
cbd-oil.egypt: CBD oil is not named anywhere in Article 73 of Egypt's customs regulations, whose only medicine rule is that medicine for personal use is part of a tourist's duty-free luggage at the discretion of the control authority. The text gives no document list. Ask Egyptian customs before bringing it.
cbd-oil.estonia: CBD oil is not named in Estonia's customs rule. If it counts as a narcotic or psychotropic medicine, you may bring one retail package of up to 30 units or 25 ml with a doctor's notice or prescription copy; more needs State Agency of Medicines authorisation. Ask the agency at Nooruse 1, Tartu, whether your product is covered.
cbd-oil.ethiopia: CBD oil is not named in the EFDA guideline. Its rule is that personal-use medical products need no pre-import permit, but the prescription is checked against what you carry. Inspectors may take samples for laboratory analysis, and a consignment suspected of containing unauthorised items is held in quarantine. Ask the EFDA beforehand.
cbd-oil.fiji: CBD oil is not named in Fiji's guideline. It says a product that is also in Schedule 1 of the Illicit Drugs Control Act 2004 needs a separate import permit from the Fiji Medicines Regulatory Authority, and a traveller must show the medicine was legally prescribed and supplied. Ask the authority whether a CBD product is covered before you travel.
cbd-oil.finland: CBD oil is not named in Finland's travel rules. Whether it counts as a medicine is a question for Fimea, the medicines agency, which the official page names for checking. If it counts as a narcotic medicine, the limit is 30 days from a Schengen country or 14 days from elsewhere. Ordering illegal medicines is a pharmaceutical offence.
cbd-oil.georgia: CBD oil is not named in Georgia's customs brochure, which says narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances may not be imported without medical documentation and that illegal import is a criminal offence. The brochure's list names codeine, methadone, methylphenidate, tramadol and others, plus everything else in Georgian law, so ask the Revenue Service about CBD.
cbd-oil.greece: CBD oil is not named in the Schengen decision that sets Greece's rule. That decision concerns narcotic or psychotropic medicine prescribed to a resident of a Schengen state: a certificate valid for 30 days at most, one drug per certificate. Whether your CBD product is covered is not stated; ask the Ministry of Health's Narcotic Drugs Division, Greece's central authority.
cbd-oil.hungary: CBD oil is not named in the Hungarian rule on controlled substances. If your product counts as one, valid documents must be shown at the customs and police check: a GP's international certificate for short amounts, or an official certificate from your country's competent authority for longer, up to 90 days.
cbd-oil.iceland: CBD oil is not named on the Icelandic Medicines Agency page. If it counts as a narcotic or psychotropic medicine, a 30-day supply, counted in defined daily doses, is the limit for non-residents. Carry a physician's certificate, the original prescription or the pharmacy label, which customs may ask for. Such medicines cannot be posted.
cbd-oil.india: CBD oil is not named in India's customs traveller guide or the CDSCO medicines notice. The guide lists narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances as prohibited articles, and the CDSCO gives them no separate rule. Ask the Indian customs before bringing it.
cbd-oil.indonesia: CBD oil is not named in BPOM's leaflet. Under Regulation 28 of 2023, narcotic medicines may not be carried in passenger belongings at all, and psychotropic medicines need a prescription and are capped at 60 days of treatment. Personal medicines enter through BPOM's Special Access Scheme. Ask BPOM before bringing it.
cbd-oil.italy: CBD oil is not named in the Italian guidance. Medicines with narcotic or psychotropic substances need an Article 75 certificate, valid for 30 days, for travellers from Schengen countries; for others, Italy's Central Narcotics Office has authorised passengers holding a similar certificate. Customs can confiscate narcotics held without authorisation.
cbd-oil.jamaica: CBD oil is not named on the Jamaica Customs FAQ, which only says items needing an import permit must get it from the Ministry of Health. The foreign ministry's prescription-drug page asks for a physician's letter, a prescription copy showing strength and quantity for your stay, and flight details. Ask Jamaica Customs, public.relations@jca.gov.jm, whether CBD needs a permit.
cbd-oil.jordan: CBD oil is not named in Jordan's traveller regulation. Where a product counts as a narcotic or psychotropic substance, the patient needs authorisations from the Narcotic and Psychotropic Substances Control Department of the Jordan Food and Drug Administration, for entering or exiting. The limit is six months and the quantity in the passenger manual.
cbd-oil.latvia: CBD oil is not named by the Latvian State Agency of Medicines. If it counts as a Schedule II or III substance, a Schengen traveller needs a certificate from the authority of the country they come from. From outside Schengen, up to 14 days (II) or 30 days (III) needs no special permit but needs a prescription or a copy.
cbd-oil.lithuania: CBD oil is not on Lithuanian customs' example lists of narcotic or psychotropic medicines. The rule is for medicines carried only for personal medical use, in original packaging and in your own name, with a certificate from a health care institution for a Schengen state or prescription copies for a non-Schengen state.
cbd-oil.malaysia: The Malaysian Traveller's Guide names cannabis as an example of a dangerous drug that must be declared on arrival, and allows only products registered with the Drug Control Authority. CBD is not named, so check the First Schedule of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952. Penalties for unregistered imports include up to RM 25,000 or three years' prison.
cbd-oil.maldives: CBD oil is not named on the Maldives Customs page. It lists narcotics and psychotropic substances as prohibited goods, with a valid prescription from a registered medical practitioner required to import controlled drugs for personal use. A cannabis-derived product should be checked with customs first.
cbd-oil.mauritius: CBD oil is not named in the Mauritius Revenue Authority's rules. If your product counts as a controlled medicine, the rule is approval from the Government Pharmacist, a legible prescription, original containers and one month at most. For other prescription medicines the limit is three months' supply.
cbd-oil.mexico: CBD oil is not named on the ANAM pages. The baggage page lets travellers bring personal medicines duty-free and requires the matching prescription for psychotropic substances, while another page lists narcotics as goods that cannot enter. Ask ANAM whether your CBD product is treated as either.
cbd-oil.nepal: We could not confirm how Nepal treats CBD oil from any official or reliable source, and we do not guess. Because cannabis-related products are restricted in many countries, ask a Nepali embassy or the Department of Drug Administration (dda.gov.np) before packing it, and carry any prescription.
cbd-oil.nigeria: We could not confirm how Nigeria treats CBD oil and we do not guess. No official traveller guideline was found. Cannabis-related products are restricted in many countries, so ask a Nigerian embassy, NAFDAC (nafdac.gov.ng) or the NDLEA before bringing it, and carry any prescription.
cbd-oil.norway: CBD oil is not named on Norway's NOMA page. If it counts as a narcotic medicine, it must be prescribed for you and documented by a prescription, medical certificate or label, and declared in the red customs zone. Without a Norwegian address, up to 30 days' use is allowed. Ask narkotikakontroll@dmp.no.
cbd-oil.philippines: CBD oil is not named in the joint circular. Its only rule for dangerous drugs and similar substances is that they fall under the Dangerous Drugs Board and PDEA regulations, with no traveller allowance. Ask PDEA whether your product is covered; anything above the circular's limits without clearance is seized and forfeited.
cbd-oil.poland: CBD oil is not named in the Polish rule we could confirm. If it contains a substance on Poland's list of narcotic drugs or psychotropic substances, you need a document from the pharmaceutical inspectorate: the Chief Pharmaceutical Inspector for countries outside the EU and Schengen area, a voivodship inspector for Schengen travel. One document per product, valid 30 days.
cbd-oil.portugal: CBD oil is not named in the Portuguese rule we could confirm. If a product contains a substance on tables I-A, II-B, II-C, III or IV of Decree-Law 15/93, you may carry it for your own use, up to 30 days of treatment, with a medical document that justifies the need. Ask Infarmed if unsure.
cbd-oil.qatar: CBD oil is not named in what we could read of Qatar's controlled-medicine system. The Ministry of Public Health requires a permit, applied for online with a valid prescription, for controlled medicines entering or leaving Qatar. Allow at least five working days, and ask the ministry whether CBD is covered.
cbd-oil.romania: CBD oil is not named on the Romanian Customs page. If a product contains a narcotic or psychotropic substance, you must declare it in writing on entering from a non-EU state, even a prescribed one. A wrong or missing declaration can bring a fine or prosecution. The page gives no quantity limit.
cbd-oil.russia: CBD oil is not named by the Russian Federal Customs Service. If a product contains narcotic or psychotropic substances, it needs medical documents in Russian, or with a notarised Russian translation, naming the medicine and quantity, and must be declared in writing. The Ministry of Health's register (GRLS) shows which registered medicines contain such substances.
cbd-oil.saudi-arabia: CBD oil is not named in the SFDA notice we could read. If it counts as a controlled drug, you need a clearance permit applied for online at cds.sfda.gov.sa, with a prescription, medical report and ID. The status shows Submitted, Completed, Rejected or Incomplete. Ask the SFDA whether CBD is covered.
cbd-oil.serbia: CBD oil is not named on the Serbian customs page. It flags medicines with controlled psychoactive substances as needing approval from the competent ministry for personal import, and the Ministry of Health website is the only contact given. Whether your CBD product counts is not stated, so ask the ministry.
cbd-oil.slovakia: CBD oil is not named in Slovakia's 2007 INCB filing. If a product contains a narcotic or psychotropic substance, a valid medical prescription is needed and the days are limited: narcotics 7 days (Schedule I) or 30 days (Schedule III), psychotropics 7 days (II) or 30 days (III and IV). The ministry is the competent authority.
cbd-oil.slovenia: CBD oil is not named on the Slovenian page. If it counts as an illicit drug used as medicine, you need a medical certificate issued or endorsed by the competent authority of your country of permanent residence, confirming you may possess it. It must be necessary for medical treatment.
cbd-oil.south-africa: CBD oil is not named in the SAHPRA guideline. SARS lists narcotics and habit-forming drugs as prohibited goods. For scheduled medicines, Regulation 8(1) allows one month's supply with a valid prescription and a prescriber's certificate. Ordering medicines from abroad needs a SAHPRA section 21 authorisation if unregistered.
cbd-oil.south-korea: CBD oil is not named on the MFDS page. Any medicine containing a narcotic or psychotropic substance needs MFDS handling approval before you enter Korea, whatever your nationality, and applications can be made online. Ask the Narcotics Policy Division, 043-719-2813, whether your CBD product is covered.
cbd-oil.spain: CBD oil is not named on the AEMPS page. If it contains a narcotic or psychotropic substance, you need an AEMPS permit to enter Spain with it, from the Narcotics and Psychotropics Area. The general limit for any traveller's medicine is three months, and the quantity must not raise suspicion of trafficking.
cbd-oil.cambodia: We could not confirm how Cambodia treats CBD oil from any source, and we do not guess. Cannabis-related products are restricted in many countries. Ask a Cambodian embassy before packing it, and carry a prescription if a doctor prescribed it.
cbd-oil.costa-rica: CBD oil is not named in the JVD requirements. If it counts as a controlled substance, you may carry one month of treatment for personal use with an ID copy, prescription, a clinical summary no older than three months, and the invoice, translated into Spanish. Longer periods are assessed case by case.
cbd-oil.cuba: Cuba's regulation prohibits cannabis, coca, cocaine and heroin in any form. CBD itself is not named, so ask the Cuban Ministry of Public Health whether your product is covered. Controlled medicines otherwise need a valid prescription, a certificate endorsed in your country of residence and one from Cuban authorities.
cbd-oil.sri-lanka: CBD oil is not named by the NMRA. Medicines in Schedule III are not permitted at all, so check whether your product is listed. Otherwise personal medicine needs no NMRA approval up to the length of your stay or 90 days, in its original container, with your prescription or records.
cbd-oil.sweden: CBD oil is not named on the Swedish Customs page. If it counts as a narcotic medicine, you may bring it only for medical purposes and personal use and must prove it with a prescription, pharmacy label or doctor's certificate. Ask Swedish Customs, +46 771 520 520, before bringing it.
cbd-oil.switzerland: CBD oil is not named by Swissmedic. If it contains a narcotic, the maximum is a 30-day supply with a certificate from where you got the medicine, one per medicine, carried in hand luggage. Non-narcotic medicines for yourself may be brought up to one month without documents.
cbd-oil.taiwan: CBD oil is not named on the Taiwan customs page. If your product is a controlled drug, you may bring up to a 6-month supply with a prescription or supporting document and a TFDA-certified statement for clearance. Non-prescription medicines are limited to 12 bottles per type and 36 in total.
cbd-oil.turkey: CBD oil is not named on the Turkish customs page, which sets no separate rule for narcotics. Medication for personal treatment is allowed in a reasonable quantity based on the length of your stay, with a medical report or doctor's prescription to show at customs. Ask Turkish customs whether CBD is treated as a medicine.
cbd-oil.china: We could not confirm how China treats CBD oil, and the 2025 psychotropic and narcotic catalogue we read does not name it. Shanghai Customs says controlled medicines must be declared and customs officers decide on site. Ask Chinese customs before bringing any cannabis-derived product.
cbd-oil.united-arab-emirates: We could not confirm how the UAE treats CBD oil. Federal Law by Decree No. 30 of 2021 makes bringing in narcotic or psychotropic substances a crime unless it is regulated medical use, and the UAE's controlled-medicines list does not name CBD. Ask the Ministry of Health before you travel.

provigil.singapore: Provigil’s modafinil is named on Appendix A of Singapore’s HSA document guide, and the related armodafinil is listed too. Both need approval before you bring them in. Apply in English at least two weeks before you arrive, and note that the approval follows the arrival date you give. You may not carry medicines for someone else, except immediate family members they were prescribed for.
provigil.china: China’s 2025 catalogue lists modafinil, the ingredient in Provigil, as a Category II psychotropic. For travellers, Shanghai Customs’ guidance is to carry prescriptions, medical records or a diagnosis certificate and to declare the medicine at the port of entry. The prescribed quantity may be extended where appropriate for Category II.
provigil.japan: Provigil’s modafinil is on the same Japanese list of psychotropics, with a quantity limit of 6 g in total that you may carry without permission or a doctor’s certificate. For more than that, or an injection form, you need a doctor’s certificate stating the illness, the reason, the medicine’s name and the quantity. More than a month’s supply goes to the ministry’s pharmaceutical inspectors by email first.

insulin.japan: Insulin is not on Japan’s list of controlled substances. A supply of up to one month, carried with its syringes or pens for your own use, needs no special procedure. For longer trips, apply online for an Import Confirmation before you fly, and carry a prescription or doctor’s note and a flight document. Syringes without the medicine need an Import Confirmation of their own.
insulin.australia: The TGA lists medicines that lower blood glucose, which includes insulin, as covered by the traveller’s exemption. You can bring up to three months’ supply for yourself or an immediate family member who travels with you. Carry a prescription or a doctor’s letter naming the medicine and dose, keep it in the original labelled packaging, and declare it to Border Force.
insulin.new-zealand: Medsafe lets a traveller carry up to three months’ supply of a prescription medicine that is not a controlled drug, and insulin is checked in Medsafe’s classification database under its ingredient name. Keep it in the original container with a copy of the prescription or a doctor’s letter. You only need to declare it on the arrival card if you carry more than three months’ worth or it was not prescribed to you.
insulin.singapore: The card for Singapore says insulin is not on the HSA list of controlled substances that need approval, so you can bring up to three months' supply without applying. Carry a copy of a valid prescription or doctor's letter from your country of residence, and keep each pen or vial in its pharmacy-labelled original container.

ozempic.japan: Ozempic’s semaglutide is not on Japan’s controlled-substances list. You may bring up to one month’s supply with its pens for your own use without any procedure. If you need more, apply online for an Import Confirmation ahead of your trip, with a prescription or doctor’s note and a flight document. Syringes without the medicine need an Import Confirmation of their own.
ozempic.new-zealand: Ozempic is semaglutide, and for New Zealand you look the ingredient up in Medsafe’s classification database. If it is a prescription medicine that is not a controlled drug, Medsafe allows up to three months’ supply carried in person. Bring a copy of the prescription or doctor’s letter and the original container. Medicines must be for you or your immediate family, and must never be sold or supplied to anyone else.
ozempic.singapore: Semaglutide, in Ozempic, is not on Singapore's HSA list of controlled substances needing approval, so a supply of up to three months is allowed without applying. Bring a valid prescription or letter from your doctor, keep each pen in its original container labelled with your name, and never bring it for anyone but an immediate family member.

wegovy.japan: Wegovy contains semaglutide, which is not on Japan’s controlled-substances list. Up to one month’s supply, brought with its pens or syringes for your own use, needs no special procedure. For a longer supply, an Import Confirmation applied for online before you travel is required, together with a prescription or doctor’s note and a flight document.
wegovy.new-zealand: Wegovy also contains semaglutide. Medsafe’s rule for a prescription medicine that is not a controlled drug is up to three months’ supply, in the original container, with a copy of your prescription or a letter from your doctor saying you are being treated with it. Declare it on the arrival card if you carry more than three months’ worth or it was not prescribed to you.
wegovy.singapore: Wegovy also contains semaglutide, which Singapore's HSA does not list among controlled substances needing approval, so up to three months' supply is allowed without applying. Carry a copy of a valid prescription or doctor's letter from your country of residence, with the dispensing label on the pack.

mounjaro.japan: Mounjaro’s tirzepatide does not appear on Japan’s controlled-substances list. Bringing up to one month of supply with its pens for your own use needs no special procedure. For more than a month, apply online for an Import Confirmation before you travel; the application needs a prescription or doctor’s note and a flight document.
mounjaro.new-zealand: For Mounjaro, the ingredient to check in Medsafe’s classification database is tirzepatide. If it counts as a prescription medicine that is not a controlled drug, you may carry up to three months’ supply for yourself or immediate family. Take the pens in their original packaging with a prescription copy or doctor’s letter. Medsafe also says such medicines must not be sold or given to others.
mounjaro.singapore: Tirzepatide, in Mounjaro, is not on the HSA's list of controlled substances that need approval, so up to three months' supply may come in without an application. You need a copy of a valid prescription or doctor's letter from your country of residence, the original labelled container, and it must be for you or an immediate family member.

benadryl.netherlands: Benadryl is not on the Dutch government’s Opium Act examples, so the general rule applies: most medicines can come into the Netherlands if you can prove they are for your own use. Keep the pack in its original packaging so that officials recognise it as a medicine. The page gives no quantity limit.
benadryl.united-states: The FDA says foreign nationals may bring a 90-day supply of drug products. For a visitor, that is the rule that covers Benadryl. If you stay longer than 90 days, more can be sent to you; the FDA suggests including evidence of personal use, such as a copy of your visa or passport, a letter from your doctor, or an English prescription. The rule differs for US citizens.
benadryl.ireland: For Benadryl, the Irish rule for visitors from outside the Schengen area is up to three months’ supply of prescription medicines for their own use, in the original packaging with your name on it. Bring the prescription or a letter from your doctor or pharmacist. Customs must be satisfied that your documents support both the amount and personal use.
benadryl.israel: Israel allows travellers to bring medicines for their own needs, up to a maximum 90-day quantity based on the recommended dosage, which is the rule for Benadryl. The Ministry of Health warns that supplements or vitamins sold over the counter elsewhere may count as medicines that need authorization in Israel. Keep the pack in its original packaging.
benadryl.austria: Benadryl is an ordinary over-the-counter product, and Austria's health ministry lets you bring your usual personal needs, up to three retail packs of the smallest size, without any permit. If a doctor prescribed it, bring a confirmation with your details, the need to continue treatment, the generic name and the dose. Keep the original packaging; a translation is advised if the note is not in German.
benadryl.brazil: Anvisa treats a medicine as personal use when the quantity fits your stay and treatment and does not look like trade. Benadryl in a normal travel amount fits that. If the amount looks too large, a prescription signed by a competent professional may be requested. Keep it in the original packaging so officers can read what it is.
benadryl.chile: Chile's customs and ISP treat medicines for you or close family as baggage in the amounts of the prescription. Benadryl is over the counter, so bring only what your stay needs. Customs counts up to six months of treatment from the prescription as reasonable use. Unlabelled powders or liquids are banned, so keep it in the original packaging.
benadryl.croatia: For other medicines such as Benadryl, Croatia's customs page allows the quantity needed for treatment, up to one month, if the medicine is approved in its manufacturer's country, together with medical documentation such as an illness history or physician's certificate. Narcotic medicines have a much shorter 5-day limit. Keep it in the original packaging.
benadryl.czechia: For an ordinary medicine such as Benadryl bought outside the European Community, the Czech Customs Administration says you may bring only the amount matching your normal personal need for your trip in the Czech Republic or the EU, for example a holiday or visit. The page sets no number of packs. Keep it in the original packaging.
benadryl.egypt: Benadryl falls under the medicine line of Egypt's Article 73 on a tourist's duty-free luggage: allowed if it is for personal use, judged by the competent control authority. The article gives no pack limit. It is listed beside personal clothing and travel items, so a small amount for your own use is the safe approach. Keep the original packaging.
benadryl.estonia: Estonia lets you carry up to 10 different medicines for personal use, up to 5 retail packages of each, without authorisation. A package is at most 200 tablets or capsules, 500 ml of oral solution, or 200 ml or 200 g for external use. These limits do not apply when you arrive from the EU-linked countries listed, such as Norway or Switzerland.
benadryl.ethiopia: Under the EFDA's 2023 guideline you need no pre-import permit for personal-use medicine such as Benadryl. The prescription from an authorised health professional must state the type, description and quantity, and officers verify the product and quantity against it at the port. Packaging should be intact and clearly labelled, since inspectors check it.
benadryl.fiji: For Benadryl, Fiji's guideline for travellers asks for evidence at the border that it was legally prescribed and supplied to you: an original or certified copy of the prescription, a signed letter from the prescriber with contact details, or a label showing you, the prescriber and the supplier with their contact details. The guideline sets no number of packs.
benadryl.finland: Finland allows prescription and self-administered medicines for personal use: up to a year's supply from an EEA country and up to three months' from outside the EEA, if the product is licensed where you bought it and bought from a licensed seller. Northern Ireland counts as EEA for this, but the rest of the UK does not. Show a prescription or doctor's certificate if asked.
benadryl.georgia: For ordinary medicines such as Benadryl, Georgia allows up to ten standard packs for personal need without medical documents, including ones not registered in Georgia. For more than ten packs you need medical documents and a daily-dose calculation for the days of your visit. The ten-pack rule excludes medicines under special control.
benadryl.hungary: Hungary says medicines that are not controlled substances need no special permit or certificate to enter the country, so ordinary Benadryl is allowed for personal use. The controlled-substance rules with certificates and 3, 30 and 90-day limits do not apply to it. Keep it in the original packaging.
benadryl.iceland: For a general medicine such as Benadryl, the Icelandic Medicines Agency allows a 100-day supply in your luggage from outside the EEA and a one-year supply from within the EEA. Customs may ask for a physician's certificate, the original prescription or a pharmacy sticker. By post from inside the EEA, up to 100 days' use is allowed.
benadryl.india: Under Rule 36 of India's Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, small quantities of a medicine for exclusive personal use may be part of your bona fide baggage, up to 100 average doses of any single drug, declared to customs if they ask. Larger amounts need a permit in Form 12-B, applied for in Form 12-A with a prescription from a registered medical practitioner.
benadryl.indonesia: For Benadryl, BPOM's leaflet allows without a prescription up to 30 pieces per product for solid medicine, or 3 pieces per product for semi-solid, liquid and aerosol forms. With a doctor's prescription you may carry what you need, up to a maximum of 90 days of treatment. Medicines are for personal use and may not be sold.
benadryl.italy: Italy's consulate guidance gives the general rule that medicines you carry have no specific requirements, which covers ordinary Benadryl for personal use. The exceptions are medicines with narcotic or psychotropic substances, which need an Article 75 certificate. Keep it in the original packaging.
benadryl.latvia: For Benadryl, Latvia requires the original packaging with the manufacturer identifiable and a purchase receipt or similar document. One shipment may cover up to 12 months of use from an EEA country, or 6 months from a third country. If you bring more than three packaging units, you must certify in writing that it is for personal use.
benadryl.lithuania: Without a doctor's certificate, Lithuania allows up to 10 packs of medicines at a time, once per calendar month, including by post; with frequent work or study trips to third countries, up to 40 packs a month in tens, with proof. If asked, the certificate must name patient, medicine, strength, quantity and duration, valid up to 6 months.
benadryl.malaysia: Malaysia lets you bring medicines, vitamins and supplements for yourself or an immediate family member travelling with you, in a quantity reasonably needed for one month's use by one person, set by the dosage label. Keep the dispensing label and original packaging. If you stay more than one month, see a registered doctor in Malaysia.
benadryl.mauritius: For prescription medicines such as Benadryl when prescribed, the Mauritius Revenue Authority asks for a legible prescription from your doctor saying the medicine is used under a doctor's direction, original containers and no more than a three-month supply. Controlled medicines have a stricter one-month limit and need approval.
benadryl.mexico: ANAM lists medicines for personal use among the items you may bring in duty-free with your baggage, together with items such as a blood pressure monitor or glucose meter. Benadryl for yourself fits that. The page does not define personal use or give a pack limit. Keep it in the original packaging.
benadryl.norway: For other medicines such as Benadryl, NOMA allows up to 3 months' use when you travel from outside the EEA and up to a year's use from within it, with proof that it is for personal use, kept in its original packaging. Doping-list medicines are limited to 30 days. Contact privateimport@noma.no or +47 22 89 77 00.
benadryl.philippines: The joint circular lets over-the-counter drugs such as Benadryl in without FDA clearance if they are for personal use and arrive in your passenger baggage, a balikbayan box or mail. The quantity should match what a prescription states, with the physician's PRC licence number or its foreign equivalent. Excess without clearance is seized and forfeited.
benadryl.russia: Under Eurasian Economic Union law, the Federal Customs Service says individuals may bring registered and unregistered medicines that contain no narcotic or psychotropic substances without showing permit documents. Benadryl falls there. To check a product's composition, look it up in the Ministry of Health's state register of medicines (GRLS). Keep the original packaging.
benadryl.serbia: For other medicines such as Benadryl, Serbian customs lets you bring the quantity needed for regular therapy for up to 15 days, for yourself or an animal travelling with you, with no medical opinion. For a larger quantity for several months of stay, up to six months, or more than one package of up to 30 dosage units, get approval from the ministry.
benadryl.slovenia: Travellers arriving from outside the EU can bring Benadryl for themselves or their family: up to three weeks for acute conditions, or for chronic conditions three weeks at the prescribed dose, and exceptionally up to 12 months with proof of permitted residence. Carry proof of prescription if it needs one.
benadryl.south-africa: The two official sources differ for Benadryl. SARS says travellers may import personal medicines for up to three months' use, with a prescription or a letter from a medical doctor, while SAHPRA's Regulation 8(1) caps scheduled medicines at one month's supply. If yours is scheduled, follow the one-month rule.
benadryl.south-korea: For other medicines such as Benadryl, South Korea allows up to 6 bottles or a 3-month supply, with proof that they are for your own use, such as a prescription, medical certificate or pharmacy label, in the original packaging. The MFDS permit rule applies only to narcotic or psychotropic medicines.
benadryl.spain: For other medicines such as Benadryl, AEMPS says the quantity must suit the prescribed treatment, must not raise suspicion of trafficking, and must not exceed three months. You may be asked for the prescription or a medical report when you enter or leave, and larger amounts are accepted only if justified. Keep the original packaging.
benadryl.sri-lanka: For Benadryl, the NMRA allows you to carry the quantity for the length of your stay or up to 90 days, whichever is less, without NMRA approval; more than 90 days needs prior approval. Keep it in its original container, or labelled with name, strength and instructions, and carry your prescription or records.
benadryl.sweden: Swedish Customs allows other medicines such as Benadryl for personal use up to three months' consumption from outside the EEA and up to one year from another EEA country, with proof such as a prescription, pharmacy label or doctor's certificate. Keep it in the original packaging.
benadryl.switzerland: Swissmedic says private individuals may import up to one month's supply of medicines that are not narcotics for their own use, so Benadryl fits. No medical certificate or other documents are required, and the amount is based on the prescription or leaflet dose. You may not import medicines for someone else.
benadryl.taiwan: For Benadryl, Taiwan's customs page allows non-prescription medicines up to 12 bottles or boxes per type and 36 in total. If it is prescription-only in Taiwan but over the counter where you bought it, the non-prescription allowance applies. Above the limits a TFDA permit is needed; keep the original packaging.
benadryl.turkey: Turkey's customs information allows a reasonable quantity of medication for personal treatment, based on the length of your stay, for Benadryl as for other medicines. Show a medical report or doctor's prescription at customs. It may be carried with you or sent one month before or three months after arrival.
benadryl.argentina: Argentina's Mercosur Resolution 66/2000 page names no drugs at all, so Benadryl's diphenhydramine is not mentioned in it. The rule it does give applies only to narcotic or psychotropic medicines: a legalised, health-authority-authorised prescription. For an ordinary antihistamine we found no limit, so keep the original packaging and ask ANMAT if you plan to carry a large supply.
benadryl.bahrain: Bahrain's filing to the UN narcotics board limits narcotics and psychotropics to 7 days, with a prescription, an endorsed doctor's certificate and a certificate from Bahrain's health authorities. Diphenhydramine is not named in it. We found no separate rule for ordinary antihistamines like Benadryl, so keep it in the original packaging.
benadryl.belgium: Belgium's medicines agency names morphine painkillers, methylphenidate, sleeping pills, methadone and buprenorphine as examples of controlled medicines, not diphenhydramine. The 3-month limit and Schengen declaration apply to those. For Benadryl we found no specific Belgian rule, so original packaging and a reasonable personal supply are the safe approach.
benadryl.bulgaria: Bulgaria's Customs Agency FAQ limits foreigners to 30 days' worth of medicines containing listed narcotic substances, with a document from the prescribing country. Diphenhydramine is not named, so Benadryl is not stated to be covered. We found no rule on ordinary antihistamines; keep the original packaging.
benadryl.cambodia: We found no official or unofficial source for Cambodia on Benadryl, so this page states no limit. Diphenhydramine is not specially restricted in most countries, but that general statement is not a Cambodian rule. Carry it in its original packaging, bring a modest personal supply, and ask a Cambodian embassy.
benadryl.colombia: Colombia's Resolution 826 of 2003, Article 59, covers narcotics and psychotropics from the 1961 and 1971 Convention lists with a 30-day limit and a prescription copy. Diphenhydramine is not on the lists we read, so Benadryl is not stated to need that. Check with a pharmacist; keep the original packaging.
benadryl.costa-rica: Costa Rica's Drug Surveillance Board rule lets treated travellers bring one month of controlled medicine with ID, prescription, an epicrisis no older than three months and an invoice, translated into Spanish. Diphenhydramine is not named, so Benadryl is not stated to need these papers. Keep the original packaging.
benadryl.cuba: Cuba's 2022 INCB filing sets amounts for narcotics and psychotropics, such as codeine 12 g and methylphenidate 1 g, with official medical documentation. Diphenhydramine is not named, so Benadryl is not stated to be covered. We found no rule on ordinary antihistamines; keep the original packaging.
benadryl.cyprus: Cyprus's Pharmaceutical Services require a permit from the Inspection Department only for internationally controlled medicines carried for your own treatment. Diphenhydramine is not named, so Benadryl is not stated to need one. We found no separate rule for ordinary antihistamines.
benadryl.denmark: Denmark's euphoriant-medicine rule allows list B to E substances up to a 30-day supply and bans list A. Diphenhydramine is not named on the agency page, so check the Executive Order's schedules if you are unsure. For Benadryl we found no separate limit. Agency phone: 44 88 95 95.
benadryl.dominican-republic: The Dominican customs manual says personal-use medicines are allowed and does not name diphenhydramine. The prescription rule applies to controlled or psychotropic substances. Benadryl is therefore not stated to need one, though customs lists medicines among items that may need a declaration. Keep the original packaging.
benadryl.france: France's ANSM says arrival needs no transport attestation and the original prescription is mandatory for medicines it covers. Diphenhydramine is not named in what we read, so Benadryl is not stated to be restricted. Keep the original packaging and, if prescribed, the prescription.
benadryl.germany: Germany's BfArM travel page concerns narcotic medicines and the Article 75 Schengen certificate, valid 30 days. Diphenhydramine is not named, so Benadryl is not stated to need it. We found no separate German limit on ordinary antihistamines; keep the original packaging.
benadryl.greece: The Schengen decision Greece cites covers narcotic and psychotropic medicines, with a 30-day certificate per drug, and names no substances. Diphenhydramine is not one we could connect to it, so Benadryl is not stated to need a certificate. We found no separate Greek rule on ordinary medicines.
benadryl.jamaica: Jamaica's government pages require a Ministry of Health permit for prescription drugs and charge duties where applicable. Diphenhydramine is not named, so whether Benadryl needs a permit is not stated. No quantity limit is given. Ask Jamaica Customs on 876 922 5140.
benadryl.japan: Japan's health ministry treats amphetamine as prohibited even with a prescription, and its Narcotics Control Department sets rules on controlled medicines. Diphenhydramine is not named in what we read, so Benadryl is not stated to be restricted. Check the ministry's guidance for any limits on quantity.
benadryl.jordan: Jordan's 2025 INCB filing covers narcotics and psychotropics: personal use, up to six months, authorisation from the Food and Drug Administration. Diphenhydramine is not named, so Benadryl is not stated to be covered. We found no rule on ordinary medicines; keep the original packaging.
benadryl.kenya: Kenya's March 2024 filing sets 30 days for narcotics and for psychotropics, with a valid prescription whose original is shown at Customs. Diphenhydramine is not named, so Benadryl is not stated to be covered. We found no separate rule on ordinary medicines.
benadryl.kuwait: Kuwait's March 2024 filing allows only substances in schedules 2, 3 and 4 and says narcotics are currently not allowed at all. It names no drugs, so diphenhydramine in Benadryl is not mentioned. We found no rule on ordinary antihistamines; ask Kuwaiti authorities if unsure.
benadryl.lebanon: Lebanon's 2014 filing allows 7 days of narcotics and 30 days of psychotropics, with approval from the Ministry of Public Health's narcotics department. Diphenhydramine is not named, so Benadryl is not stated to need approval. We found no rule on ordinary medicines.
benadryl.luxembourg: Luxembourg's March 2024 filing asks for a prescription copy and an endorsed doctor's certificate and says the Schengen agreement applies, with no day limit and no drugs named. Diphenhydramine is not named, so Benadryl is not stated to need these. Keep the original packaging.
benadryl.maldives: Maldives Customs lists narcotics and psychotropics as prohibited and asks for a registered practitioner's prescription for controlled drugs for personal use. Diphenhydramine is not named, so Benadryl is not stated to be controlled. Ask Maldives Customs if unsure; keep the original packaging.
benadryl.malta: Malta's January 2017 filing asks only for a valid medical prescription and says the Schengen agreement applies, naming no drugs and no limit. Diphenhydramine is not mentioned, so Benadryl is not stated to need it. The contact is the Superintendent of Public Health at St Luke's Hospital.
benadryl.morocco: Morocco's filing sets no day limit for controlled medicines but asks for a prescription, a patient's written request and, for medicines not sold in Morocco, an authorisation from the health authority. Diphenhydramine is not named, so Benadryl is not stated to need that. Keep the original packaging.
benadryl.nepal: We found no official or reliable source for Nepal on Benadryl, so no limit is stated. The general advice is to carry it in the original packaging with a modest supply. Nepal's Department of Drug Administration (dda.gov.np) or a Nepali embassy can confirm the current rule.
benadryl.nigeria: We found no official source for Nigeria on Benadryl, so no limit is stated. Keep the original packaging and a modest supply, and ask NAFDAC (nafdac.gov.ng) or a Nigerian embassy for the current rule before you fly.
benadryl.oman: Oman's 2016 filing gives the same 30-day limit for narcotics and psychotropics and asks for a medical report issued within six months plus the prescription. Diphenhydramine is not named, so Benadryl is not stated to be covered. We found no rule on ordinary medicines.
benadryl.panama: Panama's January 2025 filing allows up to 90 days of narcotics or psychotropics with a prescription, an endorsed doctor's certificate and an ID copy. Diphenhydramine is not named, so Benadryl is not stated to be covered. We found no rule on ordinary medicines.
benadryl.peru: Peru's January 2025 filing allows narcotics for 5 days only and psychotropics in the amount of the prescription. Diphenhydramine is not named, so Benadryl is not stated to be covered. We found no separate Peruvian rule on ordinary antihistamines.
benadryl.poland: Poland's pharmaceutical inspectorate document, issued within 15 days before crossing and valid 30 days, applies to medicines with substances on Poland's narcotic and psychotropic list. Diphenhydramine is not named, so Benadryl is not stated to need it. We found no rule on ordinary medicines.
benadryl.portugal: Portugal's Decree-Law 15/93, Article 13, allows own-use carrying of listed substances up to 30 days with a medical document. Diphenhydramine is not named in the part we could confirm, so Benadryl is not stated to be covered. We found no separate Portuguese rule on ordinary medicines.
benadryl.qatar: Qatar's Ministry of Public Health requires an online permit for controlled medicines, approved within three working days, applied for at least five working days ahead. Diphenhydramine is not named, so Benadryl is not stated to need one. We found no rule on ordinary medicines.
benadryl.romania: Romanian Customs requires a written declaration of medicines containing narcotic or psychotropic substances when entering from a non-EU state. Diphenhydramine is not named, so Benadryl is not stated to need one. We found no rule on ordinary medicines; keep the original packaging.
benadryl.saudi-arabia: Saudi Arabia's SFDA requires an online clearance permit for controlled drugs containing narcotic or psychotropic substances. Diphenhydramine is not named in the notice we could read, so Benadryl is not stated to need one. We found no rule on ordinary medicines.
benadryl.seychelles: Seychelles' December 2013 filing allows 30 days of narcotics and 90 days of psychotropics with an endorsed doctor's certificate and a Seychelles health certificate. Diphenhydramine is not named, so Benadryl is not stated to be covered. We found no rule on ordinary medicines.
benadryl.slovakia: Slovakia's 2007 INCB filing sets 7- and 30-day limits by schedule for narcotics and psychotropics, with a valid prescription. Diphenhydramine is not named, so Benadryl is not stated to be covered. The filing is old; ask the Ministry of Health, Limbova 2, Bratislava.
benadryl.thailand: Thailand's FDA sorts travellers' controlled medicines by schedule: up to 30 days with a certificate or prescription for psychotropics, 31 to 90 days with a permit. Diphenhydramine is not named in what we read, so Benadryl is not stated to be covered. Check with the Thai FDA.
benadryl.ukraine: Ukraine's March 2024 filing sets amounts such as no more than 10 ampoules of narcotics, with a prescription, customs declaration and passport. It names no drugs, so diphenhydramine in Benadryl is not mentioned. We found no rule on ordinary medicines.
benadryl.vietnam: Vietnam Customs allows medicines for your own treatment, up to 7 days' use for narcotic drugs and 10 days' for psychotropic and precursor drugs, based on the prescription. The page is dated 2019 and does not name diphenhydramine. We found no separate limit for ordinary medicines.
benadryl.new-zealand: Benadryl's diphenhydramine is not named in the New Zealand rules we read. Medsafe's general rule for prescription medicines that are not controlled is up to three months' supply, in the original container, for you or your immediate family, never to sell or supply. Look the ingredient up in Medsafe's classification database to see how it is classed.
benadryl.hong-kong: Hong Kong's Drug Office rule we read concerns dangerous drugs such as diazepam, morphine and oxycodone, which need written approval before arrival, with about 10 working days to process. Diphenhydramine is not named in it. For Benadryl we found no Hong Kong limit, so keep the original packaging and ask pharmgeneral@dh.gov.hk, 2572 2068.
benadryl.china: Shanghai Customs' advice, as we read it, concerns narcotic and psychotropic medicines, with Category I limited to the maximum quantity on one prescription and Category II extendable. Diphenhydramine is not named, so Benadryl is not stated to be covered. Customs clears medicines on personal use and a reasonable quantity.
benadryl.singapore: Diphenhydramine is not on Appendix A of Singapore's HSA document guide, the list of controlled substances needing approval. For other medicines, the HSA allows up to three months' supply with a copy of a prescription or doctor's letter, in the original container labelled by the pharmacy with your name, the medicine and the quantity.
benadryl.australia: Benadryl's diphenhydramine is not named in the Australian traveller's exemption we read, which allows up to three months' supply for yourself or an immediate family member on the trip. Carry the original dispensing label, and declare it to Australian Border Force if asked. Bringing medicines for someone else is against the law.
benadryl.canada: Diphenhydramine is not named in the Health Canada travellers' rules we read, which list controlled substances (90-day supply, in the container from your health care provider) and pseudoephedrine (3 g limit). For Benadryl we found no separate limit. Keep it in the original packaging and declare it to customs if asked.
benadryl.united-kingdom: Diphenhydramine is not named in the Home Office guidance we read, which covers Schedules 2 to 4 with a three-month limit carried on your person. For Benadryl we found no UK limit, so keep the original packaging and a reasonable personal supply.
benadryl.united-arab-emirates: Diphenhydramine is not shown on the UAE government list of controlled medicines for travellers that we read, which names items such as codeine, tramadol and pseudoephedrine and allows your stay's quantity up to three months. Benadryl is therefore not stated to be controlled, but the Ministry of Health can confirm.
